title_zh: Calendar creștin ortodox joi, 22 octombrie 2026. Rugăciunea către Sfinźii șapte tineri din Efes, rstită pentru liniște sufletească și somn odihnitor
content: Calendarul creștin ortodox pentru joi, 22 octombrie 2026, îi pomenește pe Sfinții șapte tineri din Efes, cunoscuți și sub numele de „cei șapte adormiți”. Aceștia sunt sărbătoriți de Biserica Ortodoxă de două ori pe an, pe 22 octombrie și pe 4 august. Povestea lor este legată de o peșteră din Muntele Ohlonului, unde, potrivit tradiției creștine, au dormit vreme de mai multe sute de ani. Credincioșii se pot ruga către aceștia pentru liniște sufletească și odihnă. Cine sunt Sfinții șapte tineri din Efes Sfinții șapte tineri din Efes sunt Maximilian, Exacustodian, Iamvlih, Martinian, Dionisie, Ioan și Constantin. Potrivit tradiției creștine, aceștia au trăit în vremea împăratului Deciu, când creștinii erau persecutați pentru credința lor. Pentru a se adăposti de prigoană, cei șapte tineri s-au retras într-o peșteră din Muntele Ohlonului, unde au adormit pentru mai multe sute de ani. Tot joi, 22 octombrie, Biserica Ortodoxă îl pomenește și pe Sfântul Averchie, episcopul cetății Ierapole din Frigia. În aceeași zi mai sunt pomeniți Sfântul Kukșa din Odesa, Sfântul Mucenic Alexandru episcopul, Mucenicul Iraclie, Anna, Elisaveta, Teodota și Glicheria, Sfântul Mucenic Zaharia, Sfântul Ruf și Cuviosul Lot. Rugăciunea către Sfinții șapte tineri din Efes, pentru liniște sufletească și odihnă Credincioșii care se confruntă cu griji și lipsa somnului pot rosti rugăciunea către Sfinții șapte tineri din Efes, cerând ajutor pentru dobândirea păcii sufletești. „Sfinților 7 tineri din Efes, care bine v-ați nevoit și cununa Împăratului Hristos ați dobândit, ne rugăm vouă, ca unii care multă îndrăzneală înaintea Domnului ați câștigat. Sfinților Maximilian, Exacustodian, Iamvlih, Martinian, Dionisie, Ioan şi Constantin, izbăviți-ne de lipsa somnului și puținătatea sufletului. Citește și: Gemenii Graur sunt în doliu: „Nu putem exprima în cuvinte șocul și durerea pe care le simțim.” Voi, care în vremea împăratului Deciu, prigonitorul, ați fost pregătiți să luați cununa muceniciei, mărturisind dreapta credință și împotrivindu-vă tiranului celui fără de omenie, însă, din rânduială dumnezeiască, peștera în care v-ați adăpostit nu v-a fost vouă mormânt, ci s-a făcut vouă sân al lui Avraam, în care ați dormit somn adânc mai multe sute de ani şi, ca nişte prunci ce se încălzesc la sânul maicii lor, nu ați suferit nicio stricăciune. Iar în vremea binecredinciosului împărat Teodosie, din încredințarea Mântuitorului și pentru adeverirea Învierii celei de obște, v-ați trezit și v-ați arătat oamenilor, dând mărturie despre puterea lui Dumnezeu, apoi ați adormit cu adevărat întru odihna cea veșnică. O, preaslăvită minune, încât pretutindeni oamenii o au cunoscut. Deci, și acum, când gânduri negre vin asupra noastră, văzând cum slăbim cu duhul și cum ne descurajăm din lipsa somnului, acestea ne rod și ne macină sufletește, ca un vierme neadormit. Grijile cele apăsătoare, ca niște ulii la pradă, ne covârșesc și nu mai știm ce sunt pacea și odihna încrederii în Dumnezeu. Știm că toate acestea pentru păcatele noastre sunt. Știm că, pentru puțina noastră iubire de Dumnezeu și de aproapele, în astfel de mâhniri se afundă sufletul nostru. Cu pocăință ne rugăm și cerem ajutorul vostru, Sfinților din Efes, somn binecuvântat și mângâietor, spre pacea sufletului și odihna cea trupească, dăruiți-ne. Izbăviți-ne din gândurile cele rele, iar cu cele bune ne insuflați. Scoateți-ne din grijile cele multe care ne macină și de singură grija mântuirii învățați-ne să ne ținem. Așadar, Sfinților ai lui Dumnezeu, prin ajutorul vostru, luminare și împăcare întru Hristos să găsim și cerul să îl dobândim. Amin.”

title: Félix Lungu : É muito difícil ser cristão em países fundamentais
summary: É a maior comunidade religiosa, mas também a mais perseguida do mundo. Os cristãos são notícia quase diariamente por serem alvo de ataques ou assassínios; ou por as suas instalações e símbolos terem s
summary_zh: É a maior comunidade religiosa, mas também a mais perseguida do mundo. Os cristãos são notícia quase diariamente por serem alvo de ataques ou assassínios ； ou por as suas instalações e símbolos terem s
title_zh: Félix Lungu ： É muito difícil ser cristão em países fundamentais
content: É a maior comunidade religiosa, mas também a mais perseguida do mundo. Os cristãos são notícia quase diariamente por serem alvo de ataques ou assassínios; ou por as suas instalações e símbolos terem sido danificados. Só em setembro, o Observatory on Intolerance and Discrimination against Christians dá conta de 30 casos na Europa, entre atos de vandalismo a igrejas, cemitérios, ataques a sacerdotes - um foi assassinado - ou mesmo a discriminação profissional por se ser cristão. Se a Nigéria é considerada o país mais perigoso para os católicos, o México é o inferno para padres, pois é aí que mais são assassinados. O Nascer do SOL entrevista Félix Lungu, um romeno a viver em Portugal há 31 anos, porta-voz, em Portugal, da fundação Ajuda à Igreja que Sofre (AIS). Esta organização faz relatórios sobre a liberdade religiosa no mundo, e tenta explicar onde as religiões são mais perseguidas e quais os desafios que enfrentam, com especial ênfase na Igreja Católica. Félix Langu, à semelhança dos seus chefes - a organização tem sede na Alemanha -, procura não alimentar divisões, mas é impossível fugir a factos: no Paquistão, só muito recentemente é que os empresários do lixo deixaram de recrutar obrigatoriamente cristãos; não faltam países fundamentalistas onde meninas de 10 anos são violadas e obrigadas a casar, ‘adquirindo’ automaticamente a religião islâmica; e são ainda muitas as nações onde os católicos não podem desempenhar cargos na função pública. O Vaticano calcula que, anualmente, são mortos cerca de cinco mil cristãos, mas a liberdade religiosa afeta também os muçulmanos moderados, que são alvo da ira dos fundamentalistas, acabando muitos deles assassinados. Qual o papel da Fundação Ajuda à Igreja que Sofre? A Ajuda à Igreja que Sofre, fundação Pontifícia, é uma organização que tem quase 80 anos e foi criada na Alemanha. Nasceu no final da Segunda Guerra Mundial para ajudar os refugiados alemães que se deslocavam pela Europa. Depois, pouco a pouco, ajudou cristãos dos países do Leste, por causa do comunismo, do ateísmo, de toda essa situação. Ou seja, não somos como a Cáritas, ou outras ONGs, no sentido de dar ajuda social, ou educação, ou saúde. Também chegamos a estas áreas, o foco, contudo, é a ajuda pastoral, ajudar a Igreja, ajudar sacerdotes, construir igrejas, formação de seminaristas, ajudar nas missões os missionários, com carros, com rádios, televisões, bíblias, o que é necessário para fazer a evangelização. Basicamente é isso e estamos em 24 países. A sede é na Alemanha, onde se faz a gestão de tudo isso. E nos outros 24 secretariados fazemos a angariação de fundos. Para fazer a angariação de fundos é preciso saber por que se pede dinheiro, por que se pede esta ajuda. Temos três pilares, digamos assim, da nossa missão: informar, rezar e ajudar. Informar é tentar dizer qual é a situação no mundo, sobretudo onde há carências, que tipo de carências, sempre com foco nesta dimensão pastoral ou de evangelização. Nos últimos anos, a Ajuda à Igreja que Sofre dedica-se ao estudo ou análise da situação da liberdade religiosa no mundo. Porque se nós somos uma organização da Igreja, e se temos parceiros em todo o mundo, em 186 países, é importante saber onde há carências, que tipo de carências são. E temos percebido que, por exemplo, no Médio Oriente, junto com as carências materiais, falta de escola, de saúde, da alimentação, há também esta dimensão da perseguição. Falta algo que valorizamos muito, que é a questão da liberdade religiosa, dos direitos, que estão valorizados no ocidente. O que fazem nesses países onde os cristão são perseguidos? Na Arábia Saudita, por exemplo, não há hipótese de haver uma igreja? Não, na Arábia Saudita não temos uma presença. A única presença nesses países é através da representação consular. É na capela de uma embaixada, por exemplo, de França ou de Itália, que se pode celebrar a missa, porque não há possibilidade de ter uma igreja na Arábia Saudita. Considerado o país do profeta, terra sagrada

title_zh: 十字架：所有基督徒被称为的苦难
content: By Bradlee Dean October 21, 2026 “For unto you it is given on behalf of Christ, not only to believe in Him, but also to suffer for His sake…”-Philippians 1:29 When it comes to suffering, there is not a genuine Christian who is not appointed to it. Why? For His sake. “For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus’ sake. For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ. But we have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellency of the power may be of God, and not of us. We are troubled on every side, yet not distressed; we are perplexed, but not in despair; Persecuted, but not forsaken; cast down, but not destroyed; Always bearing about in the body the dying of the Lord Jesus, that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our body. For we which live are always delivered unto death for Jesus’ sake, that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our mortal flesh. So then death worketh in us, but life in you. We having the same spirit of faith, according as it is written, I believed, and therefore have I spoken; we also believe, and therefore speak; Knowing that he which raised up the Lord Jesus shall raise up us also by Jesus, and shall present us with you. For all things are for your sakes, that the abundant grace might through the thanksgiving of many redound to the glory of God.” –2 Corinthians 4:5-15 I also realize that no one spoke of, or endured, suffering more than Christ, though ours are light in comparison (Isaiah 53), who told us before His ascension that as the Father sent Him, so He would send us (John 20:21). I have personally suffered, including fellowship with His sufferings, afflictions, trials, and testings, so that I might learn and grow from the lessons the Lord gives in the process (Psalm 119:71). Oftentimes we think we are in control of our own world; we may even deceive ourselves into believing we are trusting the Lord and are being led by His Spirit (Romans 8:14) when we are not, only to find that in the end we were all the while limiting Him through our means of control. For example, we can pray, Lord, increase our faith, or, Lord, oh, that I would grow in grace more so I might be just like you, and then, when He brings us through the process to learn the lessons, we lose control, and there it is: we find out who it is that we really are, and who it is that we really trust (John 3:6). We have heard some say that the Lord will never give us more than we can handle, and I have to say, this is not true whatsoever, because in many cases He brings us to the place of more than we can handle to show us what we cannot handle, to show us what it is that He can handle, and this with ease. This is done so that we trust not in ourselves (2 Corinthians 1: 5-10). In other words, our extremity is the Lord’s opportunity. You see, the root of fear is control, and throughout our lives we are taught to control every aspect of our lives so that we do not have to trust in the Lord (avoid suffering) that we may grow, though we claim that we are doing so. Then, when we lose that control, we have to trust the Lord in ways that we never have before, this where we suffer through our unbelief (though we hold to His Word) until we transition (by the Holy Ghost – Titus 3:5) into what it is that He means for us to be, and to see outside of our own limited controls in order to bring us into a larger place (Psalm 4:1). Isaiah 55:8-9 says, “For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the LORD. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts.” In conclusion: Through suffering, the Lord introduces us to His workings, so that we might see His faithfulness, to see His wonderful works which are His righteous operations in and through Christ, as we are confo
content_zh:
2026年10月21日 布莱德利·迪恩 “为了你们,不仅为了信仰基督,而且为了他而受苦受难。” 关于受苦,没有一个真正的基督徒没有被任命。 为什么? 为他故. " 我们不是为自己而传教,而是为主而传教;我们是你们的仆人;

因为上帝命令光从黑暗中闪出,已经照亮了我们的心,在耶稣基督面前赋予了上帝的荣耀知识之光. 但我们有这个宝藏在地上, 权力的卓越可能来自上帝,而不是我们。 我们每边都忧心忡忡,却不忧愁;我们感到困惑,但不是绝望;我们受到迫害,但不是被遗弃;

我们有着同样的信仰精神,按照它所写的,我相信,因此我说过话;我们也相信,因而也说出话来;我们知道,复活主耶稣的人,也要由耶稣来养育我们,并将我们与你一同呈现.

万事都是为你着想的,丰厚的恩典,可以通过许多为上帝所荣耀而赞颂的恩惠来达到。” ——2 科林斯人4:5-15 我也意识到,没有人会说出或忍受比基督更痛苦的事,尽管我们的比喻是轻的(以赛亚53),在他升天之前,他告诉我们,正如父亲派遣他那样,他将派遣我们(约翰20:21)。

我个人遭受了痛苦,包括同他的痛苦、苦难、考验和试验的友谊,以便我能够从上帝在这一过程中提供的经验教训(第119:71段)中吸取并成长。 我们常常认为我们控制着自己的世界;

我们甚至可以欺骗自己,使我们相信我们信任主,并且正被他的精神所引导,而我们不是那样的,我们只是发现,我们最终通过我们的控制而限制他。

例如,我们可以祈祷,主,增加我们的信仰,或者,主, 哦,我将会在恩典中成长得更多,这样我或许就和你一样,然后,当他带我们走进吸取教训的过程时,我们失去控制,这就是:我们发现我们真正是谁,我们真正信任谁(John 3:6)。

我们听到有人说,上帝永远不会给我们 超过我们所能处理, 我必须说,这不是真的,因为在许多情况下, 他带我们到我们无法处理的地方 向我们展示我们无法处理的事 向我们展示他能处理的事 以及轻松处理的事 这样做是为了让我们不信任自己(2个哥林多1:5-10).

换句话说,我们的极限是上帝的机会。 你看,恐惧的根源是控制,在我们一生中,我们被教导要控制我们生活的方方面面,这样我们不必相信主(避免痛苦),以便我们成长,尽管我们声称我们这样做了.

然后,当我们失去这种控制时,我们必须以我们以前从未有过的方式信任上帝,这是我们通过不信而受苦的地方(尽管我们坚持他的话),直到我们(由圣灵-提图斯3:5)过渡到他对我们意味着什么,并且看到我们自己有限的控制之外,以便把我们带入更大的地方(Psalm 4:1).

以赛亚55:8-9说:"耶和华说,我的想法不是你们的,你们的道路也不是我的。

因为天比地高,我的道路也比地高;我的思想也比地高。” 最后:主通过苦难向我们介绍他的工作,以便我们看见他的忠诚,看到他的出色的作品,这是他在基督中和通过基督的正义行动,就像我们聚集在一起一样。

title: De la pesadilla de Gaza al sueño de Fatma : cómo podemos seguir creyendo en la humanidad en medio del horror
summary: “I have a dream”, decía Martin Luther King en 1963, cuando agitaba las conciencias desde las escalinatas del monumento a Lincoln en Washington, en uno de los discursos más emblemáticos de la historia.
summary_zh: “我有一个梦想” ， decía Martin Luther King en 1963, cuando agitaba las conciencias desde las escalinatas del monumento a Lincoln en Washington, en uno de los discursos más emblemáticos de la historia。
title_zh: De la pesadilla de Gaza al sueño de Fatma: cómo podemos seguir creyendo en la humanidad en medio del horror
content: “I have a dream”, decía Martin Luther King en 1963, cuando agitaba las conciencias desde las escalinatas del monumento a Lincoln en Washington, en uno de los discursos más emblemáticos de la historia. Hoy, sin embargo, sólo siento ganas de decir: I have a nightmare. O mejor dicho: We have a nightmare, porque la pesadilla no sólo afecta a los palestinos, sino a todos nosotros, a cualquiera que cree que la “justicia” no es una palabra vacía. La vida de los palestinos es una pesadilla interminable. En Gaza oyes el ruido de los aviones, sientes el miedo de los bombardeos, el acecho de los drones –cada vez más traicioneros y sofisticados– que te siguen, te espían, te ensordecen y disparan. La vida cotidiana consiste en sobrevivir en tiendas de campaña desgarradas por el viento y llenas de barro. Compartir un baño con tanta gente que usarlo se vuelve imposible. Volver a una casa medio destruida por las bombas con el riesgo de que el techo se derrumbe y mate a tu familia. Afrontar el rigor del invierno –ya es el tercero desde que comenzó el genocidio–, sin ni siquiera unos libros que poder quemar para mantener a tus seres queridos, al menos a los niños y ancianos, en un lugar cálido y seguro. Sólo tiendas, frías en invierno, sofocantes en los tórridos veranos. Cuántos muertos, desplazados, huérfanos, heridos, mutilados… Y los que aún no han sucumbido al asedio total que impera desde hace más de dos años están condenados a sufrir hambre y sed, a no tener derecho a una asistencia sanitaria y a una supervivencia digna. En Cisjordania y en Jerusalén Este, los palestinos viven con el terror de despertarse en plena noche con un soldado que los apunta con un fusil a la cara, que destruye sus casas, que los amenaza, los humilla delante de sus hijos o se los lleva consigo, con sus pijamas manchados de pipí porque se han orinado encima de miedo. Mientras tanto, los colonos están cada vez más furiosos: los ataques a los pueblos, comunidades rurales, tierras, coches, ganado, están a la orden del día. Incluso en las cárceles hay casos documentados en los que se ha autorizado a periodistas y civiles israelíes a presenciar –e incluso a grabar con sus teléfonos móviles– los abusos infligidos a prisioneros palestinos, a quienes deberíamos llamar “rehenes”, dada la falta de garantías mínimas legales que caracteriza las detenciones israelíes en el territorio palestino ocupado. Esta fragmentación territorial, legal y política es la institucionalización de la excepción; es la transformación de la precariedad en condiciones permanentes; es un sistema en el que la ocupación militar y la colonización ya no son sucesos aislados, sino un régimen consolidado en el que el control no sólo se ejerce con las armas sino también mediante la planificación urbanística, la burocracia, la segmentación administrativa, con la creación de categorías jurídicas diferenciadas para personas que viven en el mismo espacio pero no bajo los mismos derechos. Y después de décadas, la violencia de esta época nos indica que hemos llegado a la fase final: la del genocidio, la de la guerra de Israel contra un pueblo que hasta ahora ha resistido como ha podido. La mujer que amasa el pan bajo los drones, el maestro que sigue enseñando bajo las tiendas, la familia que planta un limonero donde el día antes había una casa, las parejas que siguen casándose y –también en el infierno de Gaza– trayendo hijos al mundo. Es ahí donde la esperanza se vuelve radical: el sueño de un mundo que persiste y que, si nos esforzamos, puede mejorar. Este sueño es el corazón palpitante de la resistencia palestina En los últimos dos años las cosas han ido todavía a peor: el terror se ha vuelto omnipresente, cotidiano. Se trata de una pesadilla que ha alcanzado dimensiones delirantes a los ojos del mundo. Pero es cuando todo se derrumba a nuestro alrededor, entre el horror y la esperanza, que resulta indispensable comenzar a soñar. Para no sucumbir a la oscuridad de esos días, para intentar imaginar o al menos e

content:
2026 다니엘기도회 15일 간증 내가 반드시 시행하리라 강사: 최기수 목사(강원도 정선 덕천교회) 본문: 이사야 46장 11절 “내가 말하였은즉 반드시 이룰 것이요 계획하였은즉 반드시 시행하리라”.

1. 하나님께서 저를 산골 오지로 부르셨습니다

할렐루야! 저는 강원도 정선 깊은 산골 오지에서 목회하고 있는 덕천교회 최기수 목사입니다.

저희 마을에 처음 오시는 분들은 세 가지에 놀랍니다.

첫째는 대한민국에 이렇게 깊은 산골이 있다는 사실입니다. 산을 몇 개나 넘어야 마을에 도착할 수 있습니다. 마을버스도 들어오지 않고 택배도 집까지 배달되지 않습니다. 아이스크림 하나를 사려 해도 자동차로 30분을 나가야 합니다.

어르신들은 골짜기마다 흩어져 살고 계십니다. 주일이면 성도님들을 모시기 위해 차량을 운행하는데, 한 번 운행할 때 약 60km를 달립니다. 세 번을 왕복하면 180km입니다. 한두 분의 어르신을 모시기 위해 산을 넘고 또 넘습니다.

둘째는 이런 오지에 교회가 있다는 사실입니다.

셋째는 그 교회에 비교적 젊은 목사가 있다는 사실입니다.

처음 마을에 들어갔을 때 한 어르신이 저에게 말씀하셨습니다. “젊은 양반, 영업을 하려면 사람 많은 데 가서 해야지. 여기 노인네들밖에 없는데 왜 왔어?”

저는 이렇게 대답했습니다. “아버님, 아버님 때문에 제가 여기 왔습니다.”

그 어르신은 훗날 예수님을 믿고 세례를 받으셨고, 교회의 귀한 일꾼이 되셨습니다.

하나님께서는 사람이 많고 환경이 좋은 곳에만 교회를 세우시는 분이 아닙니다. 복음을 듣지 못한 한 영혼이 있는 곳에도 주님의 교회를 세우십니다.

2. 신앙의 본질을 다시 깨닫게 하셨습니다

2018년 1월, 덕천교회 전임 목사님으로부터 후임 목회자로 와 달라는 부탁을 받았습니다. 그 목사님은 일본 선교사로 부르심을 받으셨지만, 6년 동안 후임자를 찾지 못하고 계셨습니다.

저는 당시 앞으로의 사역을 위해 여러 가능성을 놓고 기도하고 있었습니다. 처음에는 선뜻 결정하지 못해 기도해 보겠다고 말씀드렸습니다.

그런데 마음에 무거운 부담이 떠나지 않았습니다. 결국 3일 동안 금식하며 기도했습니다.

금식 둘째 날, 로마서 14장 8절 말씀이 제 마음을 붙잡았습니다. “우리가 살아도 주를 위하여 살고 죽어도 주를 위하여 죽나니 그러므로 사나 죽으나 우리가 주의 것이로다”.

저는 31살에 하나님의 부르심을 받고 신학교에 들어갔습니다. 그때 저를 붙잡았던 말씀은 갈라디아서 2장 20절이었습니다. “내가 그리스도와 함께 십자가에 못 박혔나니 그런즉 이제는 내가 사는 것이 아니요 오직 내 안에 그리스도께서 사시는 것이라”.

저는 주님께서 보내시는 곳이라면 어디든 가겠다고 고백했습니다. 그러나 10년 넘는 신학 공부와 사역의 시간을 지나면서 어느새 마음이 달라져 있었습니다.

교회를 선택할 때 사례비는 얼마인지, 사택은 몇 평인지, 성도는 몇 명인지부터 생각하고 있었습니다. 어려운 시간을 견뎌 왔으니 이제는 조금 더 좋은 환경에서 사역하고 싶었던 것입니다.

그때 하나님께서 제 마음을 깨우셨습니다. 신앙의 본질은 사례비도, 사택도, 성도의 숫자도 아니었습니다. 오직 예수 그리스도였습니다. 저는 그 말씀 앞에서 회개하고 결단했습니다.

“목사님, 제가 가겠습니다.”

3. 5만 원을 통해 하나님의 살아 계심을 경험했습니다

제가 신학교에 다니던 시절에는 경제적으로 참 어려웠습니다. 학비와 기숙사비도 감당하기 어려웠고, 가족의 생계는 아내에게 맡겨야 했습니다.

어느 날 학교로 돌아가야 하는데 자동차에 넣을 기름값조차 없었습니다.

아내에게 물었습니다. “여보, 돈 좀 있어?”

그때 아내가 처음으로 어려운 형편을 이야기했습니다. “여보, 사실 아이들하고 학교에 갈 버스비가 없어서 40분씩 걸어 다니고 있어.”

그 말을 듣는 순간 마음이 무너졌습니다. 아내는 제가 더 힘들어할까봐, 그동안 아무 말도 하지 않았던 것입니다.

그날 밤 교회에서 제공한 이스타나 승합차를 몰고 학교로 향했습니다. 운전하면서 하나님께 울부짖었습니다.

“하나님, 저를 부르셨잖아요. 그런데 우리 아이들은 어떻게 합니까? 하나님, 어디 계십니까?”

그러다 자동차에 기름 경고등이 들어왔습니다. 더 이상 운전할 수 없어 여주휴게소에 차를 세웠습니다.

추운 12월 밤이었습니다. 자동차 뒷좌석에 앉아 울고 또 울었습니다. 기도조차 제대로 나오지 않았습니다. 그때 누군가 자동차 창문을 두드렸습니다. 중년의 여성 전도사님이셨습니다.

“목사님, 여기서 뭐 하세요?” 저는 기름이 떨어졌다는 말을 차마 하지 못했습니다. “조금 피곤해서 쉬고 있습니다.”

그분은 돌아가셨습니다. 저는 마음속으로 간절히 기도했습니다. “하나님, 저 좀 도와주세요. 너무 힘듭니다.”

그런데 잠시 후 그 전도사님이 다시 돌아오셨습니다. 그리고 제게 무엇인가를 건네셨습니다.

5만 원이었습니다. 저는 그 돈을 받아 들고 새벽 동이 틀 때까지 울었습니다. 그날 제게 5만 원은 500만 원, 5천만 원보다 더 귀했습니다. 단순히 기름을 넣을 돈이 생겼기 때문이 아니었습니다.

하나님께서 지금도 저를 보고 계신다는 사실을 깨달았기 때문입니다. 그릿 시냇가에서 엘리야를 먹이셨던 하나님께서 저의 작은 신음에도 응답하고 계셨습니다.

그날 저는 다시 고백했습니다. “하나님, 감사합니다. 하나님께서 저를 잊지 않으셨군요.”

4. 200년 된 집에서 새로운 목회를 시작했습니다

덕천교회에 가기로 결단한 후 아내와 함께 처음 교회를 방문했습니다.

2018년 1월, 산에는 눈이 쌓여 있었습니다. 내비게이션에도 교회가 제대로 나오지 않았습니다. 산을 넘고 또 넘어도 교회가 보이지 않았습니다.

길은 자동차 한 대가 겨우 지나갈 정도로 좁았습니다. 옆에는 절벽이 있고 고라니가 뛰어다녔습니다. 그렇게 도착한 교회는 200년 넘은 낡은 집이었습니다. 그 집에 약 6평을 덧붙여 예배당으로 사용하고 있었습니다.

처음 그 모습을 본 아내는 아무 말도 하지 못했습니다. 돌아오는 길에는 계속 울었습니다.

저는 하나님께 기도했습니다. “하나님, 저는 사명을 받았지만, 아내는 어떻게 합니까? 하나님께서 아내를 위로해 주십시오.”

아내도 3일 동안 기도했습니다. 그런데 어느 날 아내가 환한 얼굴로 나왔습니다. 하나님께서 말씀으로 위로해 주셨다는 것입니다.

요한일서 3장 18절이었습니다. “자녀들아 우리가 말과 혀로만 사랑하지 말고 행함과 진실함으로 하자”.

아내는 제게 이렇게 말했습니다. “여보, 우리가 말로만 주님을 사랑한다고 하면 안 되잖아. 이제 행함과 진실함으로 주님을 사랑하자.”

그렇게 우리는 덕천교회로 들어갔습니다. 하지만 생활은 생각보다 훨씬 어려웠습니다. 낡은 집에는 쥐가 많았고 뱀까지 나타났습니다. 천장에서는 쥐들이 뛰어다녔고, 신발 속에서도 뱀이 발견되었습니다.

예배당에는 여섯 분의 어르신이 계셨습니다. 대부분 신앙생활을 시작한 지 얼마 되지 않은 분들이었습니다. 설교 중에 서로 다투기도 하셨습니다. 그런데 1년 반이 지나자 두 분은 돌아가시고, 두 분은 요양원으로 가셨습니다.

목회가 무엇인지, 어떻게 해야 하는지 막막했습니다. 사례비도 없었습니다. 부모님과 형제들, 선배 목사님들이 보내주시는 후원금이 한 달에 약 59만 원이었는데, 겨울철 전기요금만 68만 원이 나왔습니다.

그러나 하나님께서는 그곳에서도 우리를 먹이시고 입히셨습니다.

5. 목회는 한 영혼의 삶 속으로 들어가는 것이었습니다

처음 덕천교회에 부임했을 때 가장 어려웠던 것은 지역에 깊이 자리잡은 무속신앙이었습니다. 마을에는 신성하게 여기는 나무가 있었고, 무속인들은 교회가 들어와 마을에 부정이 탄다고 이야기했습니다.

전도하러 가면 냉대받기 일쑤였습니다. 술에 취한 분이 막대기를 휘두르기도 했습니다. 저는 부임한 지 3개월 만에 지쳐 버렸습니다. 그때 하나님께 부르짖었습니다.

“하나님, 저를 이곳에 보내셨는데 어떻게 목회해야 합니까? 제 힘으로는 감당할 수 없습니다.”

기도하던 중 요한복음 21장 말씀이 마음에 다가왔습니다. 부활하신 예수님께서 베드로에게 말씀하셨습니다.

“네가 나를 사랑하느냐.”

그리고 주님은 양들을 먹이고 돌보라고 명령하셨습니다.

title_zh: 【2026但以理祷告会：第13天】金宇俊牧师“在医院经历的最大恩典”
content:
2026 다니엘기도회 13일차 간증 모든 것을 잃으면 비로소 보이는 것 강사: 김우준 목사(분당 지구촌교회) 본문: 골로새서 2장 6-7절

1. 신앙생활의 본질을 잃어버린 그리스도인들

사랑하는 성도 여러분! 오늘 여러분과 함께 우리의 신앙생활을 돌아보고 싶습니다. 혹시 이런 생각을 해보신 적이 있습니까? 성경이 말하는 참된 신앙생활과 우리가 실제로 살아가는 모습은 왜 이렇게 다를까요?

성경이 말하는 신앙생활은 살아 계신 하나님과 생동감 있게 동행하는 삶입니다. 전능하신 하나님께서 언제 어디서나 나와 함께하신다는 사실을 진정으로 믿는다면 우리의 삶에는 감사와 기쁨과 평강이 넘쳐나야 합니다. 그런데 실제 우리의 모습은 어떻습니까? 많은 그리스도인이 걱정과 근심과 염려에 시달리며 살아갑니다.

성경은 우리가 그리스도의 장성한 분량에 이르기까지 예수님을 닮아가야 한다고 가르칩니다. 그런데 우리의 모든 생각과 말과 행동이 공개된다면, 주변 사람들이 우리를 보면서 예수님을 닮았다고 말할 수 있을까요?

우리의 지난 일주일을 돌아보십시오. 가정과 직장에서 하나님의 나라를 얼마나 생각하며 살아왔습니까? 혹시 하나님 나라를 생각할 겨를도 없이, 자신의 문제와 계획에만 몰두하지는 않았습니까?

저는 오늘날 많은 그리스도인의 삶이 무기력해진 근본적인 이유가 신앙의 첫 단추를 잘못 끼웠기 때문이라고 생각합니다. 신앙의 가장 중요한 본질을 놓쳐버린 것입니다. 그렇다면 우리가 절대로 놓쳐서는 안 되는 신앙생활의 본질은 무엇입니까?

골로새서 2장 6-7절은 말씀합니다. “그러므로 너희가 그리스도 예수를 주로 받았으니 그 안에서 행하되 그 안에 뿌리를 박으며 세움을 받아 교훈을 받은 대로 믿음에 굳게 서서 감사함을 넘치게 하라”.

참된 신앙생활은 예수님을 내 삶의 주인으로 모셔드리는 것에서 시작됩니다. 그분 안에서 살아가고, 그분 안에 뿌리를 내리며, 믿음에 굳게 서서 감사함이 넘치는 삶을 살아가는 것입니다. 예수님을 믿는다는 것은 한마디로 인생의 주인이 바뀌는 것을 의미합니다.

2. 예수님을 믿는다는 것은 인생의 주인이 바뀌는 것입니다

사도행전 16장 31절에서 바울은 빌립보 감옥의 간수에게 말했습니다. “주 예수를 믿으라 그리하면 너와 네 집이 구원을 받으리라”. 로마서 10장 9절에서도 예수님을 주로 시인하고 하나님께서 그를 죽은 자 가운데서 살리신 것을 마음에 믿으면 구원을 받는다고 말씀합니다.

베드로전서 3장 15절은 마음에 그리스도를 주로 삼아 거룩하게 하라고 가르칩니다. 빌립보서 2장 11절은 모든 입으로 예수 그리스도를 주라 시인하여 하나님 아버지께 영광을 돌리게 하셨다고 선포합니다. 고린도전서 12장 3절은 성령으로 아니하고는 누구든지 예수를 주시라 할 수 없다고 말씀합니다. 고린도후서 4장 5절에서 사도 바울은 자신을 전파하는 것이 아니라 그리스도 예수의 주 되신 것을 전파한다고 고백합니다.

성경은 이처럼 예수 그리스도의 주 되심을 강조합니다. 예수님을 믿는다는 것은 단순히 종교적인 지식을 받아들이거나 교회에 출석하는 것이 아닙니다. 예수님을 내 인생의 주인으로 인정하고 그분의 다스리심 가운데 살아가는 것입니다.

그런데 여기서 중요한 문제가 있습니다. 우리는 입술로는 예수님을 주님이라고 고백합니다. 그러나 실제 삶에서는 여전히 자신이 주인으로 살아갑니다. 내 인생의 소유권도 내가 가지고 있고, 결정권도 내가 행사하며, 경영권도 내가 놓지 않으려고 합니다.

여러분에게 묻고 싶습니다. 여러분의 인생의 주인은 정말 예수 그리스도이십니까? 그렇다면 삶의 모든 소유권과 결정권을 주님께 내어드리셨습니까?

예를 들어 제가 가지고 있던 책 한 권을 누군가에게 선물했다고 생각해 보십시오. 그 책을 선물한 순간부터 소유권은 누구에게 있습니까? 당연히 선물받은 사람에게 있습니다. 처음에는 절반만 소유권을 넘기고 시간이 지나면서 조금씩 나머지를 넘기는 것이 아닙니다. 주인이 바뀌는 순간 소유권도 바뀝니다.

우리 신앙생활도 마찬가지입니다. 예수님을 주님으로 모셨다면 내 삶의 주인이 바뀐 것입니다. 그런데 우리는 예수님을 주님이라고 부르면서도 여전히 내 뜻대로 살려고 합니다. 예수님은 부분적인 헌신이 아니라 전인격적인 헌신을 요구하십니다.

물론 이것이 우리의 행위나 헌신으로 구원을 얻는다는 뜻은 아닙니다. 구원은 오직 예수 그리스도의 은혜로 받습니다. 그러나 예수님을 믿는 사람에게는 자신의 삶을 주님께 맡기려는 마음의 결단이 있어야 합니다. 누구든지 예수님께 나아올 수 있습니다. 그러나 예수님을 주님으로 인정하지 않은 채 자기 뜻만을 고집하는 태도는 참된 믿음의 자세가 아닙니다.

3. 중증 근무력증, 모든 것이 무너졌던 그날

저 역시 이 사실을 머리로는 잘 알고 있었지만, 실제 삶에서 받아들이기까지는 너무 오랜 시간이 걸렸습니다. 제가 미국 텍사스에서 신학 공부를 하던 시절이었습니다. 당시 저는 공부와 직장생활, 사역을 동시에 감당하고 있었습니다. 하루하루가 치열했습니다.

그러던 어느 날 직장에서 일하고 있는데 갑자기 눈과 얼굴에 마비 증상이 나타났습니다. 눈꺼풀이 너무 무거워서 잠시도 눈을 뜨고 있을 수 없었습니다. 처음에는 과로 때문이라고 생각했습니다. 충분히 쉬면 괜찮아질 것이라고 여겼습니다. 그러나 며칠이 지나고 2주가 지나도 증상은 나아지지 않았습니다. 병원에서 여러 검사를 받은 후, 의사로부터 중증 근무력증이라는 진단을 받았습니다.

생명을 위협할 수 있는 심각한 질환이라는 설명을 들었습니다. 미국의 비싼 의료비를 감당하기 어려웠던 저는 서둘러 한국으로 돌아왔습니다. 고려대학교병원에서 다시 정밀검사를 받았습니다. 검사 결과를 확인한 신경과 전문의는 제게 매우 충격적인 이야기를 했습니다.

제 상태가 심각하고, 마비가 빠르게 진행될 수 있다는 것이었습니다. 앞으로 6개월 안에 전신이 마비될 수 있으며, 호흡근까지 마비된다면 생명도 위험할 수 있다는 설명이었습니다. 당시 의사는 치료가 매우 어렵다고 말하며, 즉시 입원할 것을 권했습니다.

저는 그 말을 도저히 받아들일 수 없었습니다. 이제 막 하나님께서 부르신 사명을 감당하려고 준비하고 있는데, 앞으로 전신이 마비되어 침대에 누워 살아야 할 수도 있다니, 이해할 수 없었습니다. 병실 침대에 앉아 창밖을 바라보았습니다. 한참 동안 아무 말도 할 수 없었습니다. 그러다가 하나님께 기도하기 시작했습니다. 그러나 그것은 기도라기보다 원망에 가까웠습니다.

“하나님, 왜 저에게 이런 고난을 허락하십니까? 제 인생을 이렇게 끝내실 것이었다면 왜 저를 사역자로 부르셨습니까? 이제부터 세상으로 나아가 복음을 전해야 하지 않습니까? 하나님 영광을 위해 쓰임받지도 못하고 평생 침대에 누워 가족들에게 짐이 되어야 한다면, 차라리 지금 제 생명을 가져가십시오.”

저는 하나님을 원망했습니다. 물론 하나님께서 언제나 저와 함께하신다는 사실을 알고 있었습니다. 신학적으로도 충분히 설명할 수 있었습니다. 그러나 그 순간만큼은 하나님 한 분만으로 충분하다는 고백을 할 수 없었습니다.

제게는 하나님에 더해서, 건강이 있어야 행복할 것 같았습니다. 건강을 잃는다면, 적어도 돈이라도 있어야 안심할 수 있을 것 같았습니다. 평생 누군가의 도움을 받아야 한다면 경제적 여유라도 있어야 하지 않겠습니까? 그동안 수없이 하나님 한 분만으로 충분하다고 고백했지만, 막상 모든 것을 잃을 수 있는 상황에 놓이자 그 고백이 무너졌습니다.

4. 욥의 고백 앞에서 깨달은 하나님의 소유권

바로 그때 하나님께서 한 성경 말씀을 제 마음에 떠오르게 하셨습니다. 욥기 1장 21절입니다. “주신 이도 여호와시요 거두신 이도 여호와시오니 여호와의 이름이 찬송을 받으실지니이다”.

그 말씀 앞에서 저는 비로소 깨닫게 되었습니다. 저는 그동안 제 몸만큼은 제 것이라고 생각했습니다. 제 팔과 다리를 움직이는 것, 제 발로 걸어 다니는 것, 제 손으로 밥을 먹는 것은 당연히 누려야 할 권리라고 여겼습니다. 그러나 그날 병실에서 깨달았습니다. 제가 누리고 있던 건강과 시간, 손과 발, 그리고 마지막 호흡까지 어느 하나 당연한 것이 없었습니다. 모두 하나님께서 허락하신 은혜였습니다.

저는 그 모든 것을 잠시 맡아 관리하는 청지기에 불과했
content_zh:
2026年但以理祷告会第13天见证 失去一切后才能看到的东西 讲员：金宇俊牧师（盆唐地球村教会） 经文：歌罗西书2章6-7节

1. 失去信仰生活本质的基督徒

亲爱的弟兄姊妹们！今天我想与大家一起回顾我们的信仰生活。您是否曾有过这样的想法？为什么圣经所说的真正的信仰生活与我们实际的生活方式有这么大的差别呢？圣经所说的信仰生活，是与活着的上帝充满活力地同行的人生。如果我们真心相信全能的神随时随地与我们同在，那么我们的生活就应该充满感恩、喜乐与平安。然而，我们实际的样子又如何呢？许多基督徒在忧虑、烦恼和焦虑中度日。

圣经教导我们，要效法耶稣，直到达到基督长成的身量。但是，如果我们的所有思想、言语和行为都被公开，周围的人看到我们时，会说我们像耶稣吗？回想一下我们过去的一周。在家庭和工作场所，您在多大程度上想着神的国度而生活？您是否没有时间去想神国，只是一心扑在自己的问题和计划上？我认为，如今许多基督徒的生活变得软弱无力的根本原因，在于他们一开始就走错了信仰的道路。他们错过了信仰最重要的本质。那么，我们绝不能忽视的信仰生活的本质是什么呢？歌罗西书2章6-7节说：

“所以你们既领受了主基督耶稣，就当遵他而行，在他里面生根建造，信心也得以坚固，正如你们所学的，感谢的心也更增长了。” 真正的信仰生活始于尊耶稣为主宰我的生命。就是在祂里面生活，在祂里面扎根，在信仰上站稳，过着充满感恩的生活。简而言之，相信耶稣意味着人生主人发生了变化。2. 信耶稣就是改变人生之主

在《使徒行传》第16章31节中，保罗对腓立比监狱的狱卒说：“当信主耶稣，你和你一家都必得救。”

罗马书10章9节也说，你若口里认耶稣为主，心里相信神叫祂从死里复活，就必得救。彼得前书3章15节教导我们要尊主基督为圣。腓立比书2章11节宣告，叫各人（包括天使、人、鬼魔）认耶稣基督为主，归荣耀给父神。哥林多前书12章3节说，若不是被圣灵感动的，就没有人能说“耶稣是主”。在哥林多后书4章5节中，使徒保罗承认他所传扬的不是自己，而是耶稣基督为主。圣经就是这样强调耶稣基督的主的身份。相信耶稣不仅仅是接受宗教知识或去教会。

就是承认耶稣是我生命的主，并在祂的管治之下生活。但是，这里有一个重要的问题。我们用嘴唇承认耶稣为主。但在现实生活中，我们仍然以自己为主。我拥有自己的人生，我行使自己的决定权，我也不想放弃自己的掌控权。我想问问大家，你们生命的主人真的是耶稣基督吗？如果是这样，您是否已经将生活中所有的所有权和决定权都交给了主？举个例子，想象一下我把一本我拥有的书送给某人。从我把这本书送出去的那一刻起，这本书的所有权归谁所有？当然是在收到礼物的人那里。

这不是一开始只转让一半所有权，然后随着时间的推移一点一点地转让剩下的部分。主人一变，所有权也会随之改变。我们的信仰生活也是如此。如果我以耶稣为主，那么我生命的主人就变了。然而，我们虽然称耶稣为主，却仍然想要按照自己的意思生活。耶稣要求的是全人的委身，而不是部分的委身。当然，这并不意味着我们可以通过自己的行为或奉献来获得救恩。救恩只能通过耶稣基督的恩典来获得。但是，信耶稣的人必须有将自己的生命交托给主的内心决心。任何人都可以来到耶稣面前。然而，不承认耶稣为主，只坚持己意的态度并不是真信心的态度。3.

重症肌无力，一切崩塌的那一天

我也在脑海里清楚地知道这个事实，但花了很长时间才在现实生活中接受它。那是我在美国德克萨斯州攻读神学的时候。当时，我同时兼顾着学业、工作和侍奉。每一天都过得很辛苦。有一天，我在工作时突然感到眼睛和面部麻痹。我的眼睑太沉重了，连一小会儿都无法睁开眼睛。起初，我以为这是因为过度劳累。我以为只要好好休息一下就会好起来。然而，过了几天，又过了两周，症状还是没有好转。在医院做了多项检查后，医生诊断我患有重症肌无力。

我被告知这是一种可能危及生命的严重疾病。由于我无法负担美国高昂的医疗费用，我匆忙回到了韩国。我在高丽大学医院再次接受了全面检查。看过检查结果的神经科专科医生告诉我一个非常令人震惊的消息。他说我的病情很严重，麻痹可能会迅速恶化。他解释说，在接下来的6个月内，我可能会全身瘫痪，如果呼吸肌也瘫痪，我的生命也可能会有危险。当时，医生说治疗非常困难，并建议我立即住院。我实在无法接受他说的话。我刚刚准备好去履行上帝赋予我的使命，却得知自己将来可能会全身瘫痪，只能躺在床上度过余生，我实在无法理解。

我坐在病房的床上，望着窗外。好久都说不出话来。然后我开始向神祷告。但那更像是怨恨，而不是祷告。“神啊，您为什么让我遭受这样的苦难？如果您要让我的人生以这样的方式结束，那您当初为什么要召我成为传道人呢？难道我不是应该从现在开始走向世界去传福音吗？如果我不能为主的荣耀而被使用，而是要一辈子躺在床上成为家人的负担，那还不如现在就取走我的性命吧。”

我怨恨神。当然，我知道神一直与我同在。从神学的角度，我也能做出充分的解释。然而，在那一刻，我无法坦承只有神一位就足够了。

对我来说，除了有神之外，还需要有健康才能感到幸福。如果失去了健康，我觉得至少得有钱才能安心。如果一辈子都要依靠别人的帮助，那至少也得有经济能力吧？在此之前，我无数次地宣告说，唯有神就足够了，但当我真的面临可能失去一切的境地时，这个宣告就崩溃了。4. 在约伯的告白面前认识到神的所有权

就在这时，神让我想起了一句圣经的话。《约伯记》第1章第21节：“赏赐的是耶和华，收取的也是耶和华；耶和华的名是应当称颂的。” 面对这句话，我终于明白了。我一直以为至少我的身体是属于我的。

我曾认为，能够活动自己的胳膊和腿、用自己的双脚走路、用自己的双手吃饭，是理所当然的权利。然而，那天在病房里我明白了。我所拥有的健康、时间、手脚，甚至最后一口气，没有一样是理所当然的。这一切都是上帝赐予的恩典。我只是一个暂时负责管理这一切的管家。

summary_zh: 文：马克·埃利斯（Mark Ellis）——安珀·斯帕克斯（Amber Sparks）在加利福尼亚州拉古纳海滩长大，对海洋产生了深厚的热爱，这促使她在加州大学伯克利分校学习海洋科学，并在圣地亚哥的斯克里普斯研究所获得了硕士学位。作为蓝纬度基金会的联合创始人，她与业界合作，寻找保护机会，[…]  这篇题为《蝠鲼引导海洋科学家找到失去的鳍》的文章最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
title_zh: 蝠鲼带领海洋科学家找到失去的鳍
content: By Mark Ellis — Amber Sparks (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook page) Growing up in Laguna Beach, California, Amber Sparks developed a deep love for the ocean, which led her to study marine science at UC Berkeley and earn a master’s degree at Scripps Institute in San Diego. As co-founder of Blue Latitudes Foundation, she works with industry to find opportunities for conservation, especially with the Rigs-to-Reefs program, when oil drilling platforms are decommissioned. “We work with the oil companies to repurpose certain parts of the platform, retrofit it so that it can remain in place and continue to function as an artificial reef,” she told God Reports. Amber’s work has taken her around the world, with many dive experiences and encounters in the ocean with marine life. But there is one story she will never forget. It happened in the Gulf of Mexico shortly after Amber graduated from Scripps Institute and was invited on a research industry cruise with oil company representatives, scientists, and regulators on a liveaboard vessel. At the Flower Garden National Banks, a marine protected area 200 miles offshore, Amber was excited about her first dive, but slightly nervous. “You don’t know what you’re going to see or what this experience is going to be like,” she recalls. Dropping in (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook) Each diver had to jump off the vessel to get in the water. “We’re all geared up with our snorkel, our buoyancy control device, our wetsuit, and fins are the last thing you put on. So, I put on my fins and I jumped off the side of the boat.” “The second that I hit the water, one of my fins fell off, and I looked down and watched as it slowly descended to the bottom.” Amber glanced over at her dive buddy, and said, “I’m gonna go down. I’m going down.” Normally she would wait for her dive partner and they would go down together, but in this case, she thought, “I can’t (wait). I gotta go get my fin.” So Amber slowly began to descend to the bottom, about 60 feet below the ocean surface. “I felt completely lost. I was in a completely new area. I never dove before, and now I only had one fin.” She realized there were major currents that could have moved her fin in any direction. “I realized I can’t really swim with just one fin. So now not only am I at depth, but I’m handicapped with just one fin, and I started to feel pretty nervous.” It would probably take her 10 minutes to get back the surface, with safety stops. At the moment before panic set in, she looked upward and saw an amazing sight. It was a giant manta ray, with wings extending at least 10 feet. “Its wingspan was double mine. Its arms were out, and it was coming up over the side of a reef. “I’ve never seen a manta ray like this before. It totally took my breath away, it was so magnificent.” Another manta ray (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook page) She noted that manta rays are known in the ocean community to be “majestic, God-connected creatures with an understanding maybe beyond what humans can fully comprehend. They see the world and feel it in another way,” she notes. Mantas have the largest known brain of any fish. Their brains are large in absolute terms and relative to body size, which is also true of elephants, dolphins, and people. Their brains have enlarged areas associated with intelligence, vision, and motor coordination, and some of their brain cells are more like those in birds and mammals than in other fish.(1) As the manta ray drew close to Amber, she had an unusual communication experience. “I felt this sense where it said, ‘I want you to follow me. I’m going to help you find your fin.’ Amber Sparks Amber’s diving partner had just descended next to her, and they both began to swim after the manta. “I was barely making it, following this manta ray across the reef. At this point, I was so excited to see a manta ray. I kind of forgot about being handicapped, and I was just trying to go as fast as I can to keep up with it. Then Amber got the sur

title: Lanier’s Sixth Annual John Warwick Montgomery Lecture Series: A Grand Success
summary: While sitting in the John Warwick Montgomery Study Center at the Lanier Library and Study Center in Houston, Texas, awaiting a meeting, I turned to librarian Sharon Cofran and Executive Director Dr. David Fleming and remarked, “John Warwick Montgomery would be very pleased with what Lanier has accomplished on his behalf.” From Montgomery’s framed correspondence […]  The post  Lanier’s Sixth Annual John Warwick Montgomery Lecture Series: A Grand Success  first appeared on  God Reports .
summary_zh:
在德克萨斯州休斯顿拉尼尔图书馆和研究中心的约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利研究中心等待开会时,我转而请图书管理员莎伦·科夫兰和执行主任Dr.

大卫·弗莱明(David Fleming)说,“约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利(John Warwick Montgomery)将非常满意拉尼尔代表他取得的成就。” 蒙哥马利的书信[.] Lanier的第六届年度John Warwick Montgomery讲座系列:大成功首次出现在上帝报告上。
title_zh: 拉尼尔第六届年度约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利系列讲座：圆满成功
content: John Warwick Montgomery While sitting in the John Warwick Montgomery Study Center at the Lanier Library and Study Center in Houston, Texas, awaiting a meeting, I turned to librarian Sharon Cofran and Executive Director Dr. David Fleming and remarked, “John Warwick Montgomery would be very pleased with what Lanier has accomplished on his behalf.” From Montgomery’s framed correspondence with C. S. Lewis and his barrister gowns to the thousands of books that comprise his remarkable personal collection, Lanier has provided the Christian world with a marvelous tribute to one of the great Christian intellectuals of the twentieth and twenty-first centuries. Born in 1931, John Warwick Montgomery (d. 2024) was a distinguished Christian apologist, theologian, attorney, and scholar whose extraordinary career spanned several disciplines. Holding numerous academic degrees, including doctorates in theology, philosophy, and law, Montgomery became internationally recognized for his defense of Christianity through historical evidence, legal reasoning, and philosophical argumentation. His influential books, including History and Christianity , Faith Founded on Fact , and The Shape of the Past , helped establish a rigorous approach to Christian apologetics. Whether lecturing in universities, debating skeptics, or practicing law, Montgomery maintained that Christianity was not merely a matter of subjective belief but a faith grounded in historical reality and rational inquiry. Yet to stop at the library would be to understate Lanier’s remarkable work. The sixth annual John Warwick Montgomery Lecture Series was a tour de force of distinguished thinkers, passionate Christians, and intellectually engaging presentations. More than a commemoration of Montgomery’s life, the gathering represented a continuation of his intellectual legacy: the conviction that Christianity can withstand serious scrutiny and offer compelling answers to life’s most profound questions. Mark Lanier, Nancy Pearcey, Paul Gould, Adam Francisco, and Michael Horton From the opening panel discussion hosted by attorney and philanthropist Mark Lanier to Dr. Paul Gould’s thoughtful presentation on worldviews, followed by attorney Craig Parton’s lecture on jurisprudential apologetics, one theme emerged with unmistakable clarity: Christianity is a reasonable faith. The presentations reflected Montgomery’s own interdisciplinary approach to apologetics: the Christian faith and intellectual inquiry need not be adversaries. Indeed, the Christian tradition has long insisted that faith and reason are complementary avenues in the pursuit of truth. The following day continued this rich intellectual exploration. Professor Nancy Pearcey addressed questions surrounding truth, dismantling various modern ideologies, while Dr. Adam Francisco offered an informative overview of Islamic history and belief, helping participants better understand one of world’s biggest religions. The keynote address by Dr. Michael Horton examined the challenge of reaching those who identify as “spiritual but not religious,” a growing segment of contemporary society. Horton’s presentation underscored the importance of communicating historic Christian truth in a culture increasingly suspicious of religious institutions yet often deeply interested in spiritual meaning. Dr. Michael Horton On Sunday morning, Lanier founder, Mark Lanier, hosted many participants during his Biblical literacy class, where he continued the dialogue with Michael Horton. Taken together, the lectures, discussions, and interviews demonstrated the breadth of Christian scholarship and the continuing relevance of thoughtful apologetics in an age of skepticism, religious pluralism, and cultural uncertainty. As I reflected on the weekend, I was reminded of the Festschrift Christianity for the Tough-Minded , a collection of scholarly essays honoring Montgomery’s life and ministry. Like that volume, the Lanier lecture series brought together diverse intellec
content_zh:
约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利 在德克萨斯州休斯敦拉尼尔图书馆和研究中心的约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利研究中心等待开会时,我找图书管理员沙龙·科夫兰和执行主任戴维·弗莱明博士说:“约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利将非常高兴拉尼尔代表他取得的成就。” 蒙哥马利与C.S.的书信

刘易斯和他的大律师礼服为他杰出的个人收藏的数千本书,为基督教世界向20世纪和21世纪伟大的基督教知识分子之一致敬。 1931年出生于约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利(d.

2024年)是一位杰出的基督教道歉学家,神学家,律师和学者,其非凡的事业跨越多个学科. 蒙哥马利拥有众多学术学位,包括神学,哲学和法学的博士学位,他通过历史证据,法律推理,哲学论证,为基督教辩护而获得国际承认.

他的有影响力的著作,包括历史和基督教、基于事实的信仰、以及过去的造型,帮助确立了对基督教学的严格态度。 无论是在大学里讲课,辩论怀疑论,还是执业法律,蒙哥马利都坚持认为基督教不仅仅是主观信仰的问题,而是建立在历史现实和理性调查基础上的信仰.

然而, 停留在图书馆将会低估拉尼尔的出色工作。 第六届年度约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利讲座系列是由杰出的思想家,充满热情的基督徒,以及智力参与的演讲组成的巡回演出.

这场集会不仅仅是纪念蒙哥马利的一生,它代表着他思想遗产的延续:相信基督教能够经受住严肃的审视,为人生最深刻的问题提供令人信服的答案.

马克·拉尼尔 南希·皮尔西 保罗·古尔德 亚当·弗朗西斯科 迈克尔·霍顿 从律师和慈善家马克·拉尼尔主持的开场小组讨论到保罗·古尔德博士关于世界观的深思熟虑的演讲,然后是克雷格·帕顿律师关于法学理论的演讲,一个主题以明确无误的方式出现: 基督教是一种合理的信仰.

这些介绍反映了蒙哥马利自己对学说采取的跨学科方法:基督教信仰和知识调查不必是对手。 事实上,基督教传统长期以来一直坚持信仰和理性是追求真理的补充途径。 次日继续进行这种丰富的知识探索.

Nancy Pearcey教授谈到了围绕真理的问题,摧毁了各种现代意识形态,而Adam Francisco博士则提供了伊斯兰历史和信仰的翔实概览,帮助与会者更好地理解世界上最大的宗教之一。 由Dr.A.先生作主旨发言。

迈克尔·霍顿研究了帮助那些认为是“精神上但并非宗教上”的当代社会日益扩大的阶层的挑战。 霍顿的演讲强调了在一种对宗教机构越来越怀疑、但往往对精神意义很感兴趣的文化中传播基督教历史真理的重要性。 医生

迈克尔·霍顿 星期天早上,拉尼尔创始人马克·拉尼尔(Mark Lanier)在他的圣经识字课期间接待了许多参与者,在那里他继续与迈克尔·霍顿进行对话.

summary_zh: 文：查尔斯·加德纳（Charles Gardner）——在第二次世界大战南太平洋的一场海战中，一名日本水兵所在的驱逐舰被美国人击沉，他的大多数战友都淹死了。令人惊奇的是，尽管鱼雷官新谷通晴与其他人一起被卷入波涛之下，随着战舰的沉没，但他却奇迹般地在这场1942年的灾难中幸存下来。（只有18名……）  这篇文章《二战日本战俘在战俘营中找到“自由”》最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
title_zh: 二战日本战俘在战俘营中找到“自由”
content: By Charles Gardner — When a Japanese sailor’s destroyer was sunk by the Americans in a World War II South Pacific battle, most of his companions drowned. Amazingly, even though he was sucked underneath the waves with others as the ship went down, torpedo officer Michiharu Shinya somehow survived this 1942 disaster. (Only 18 of the 200-strong crew did). But he would rather have died at that point as his people had been indoctrinated to believe that it was shameful to be captured. Nevertheless, he was badly wounded but nursed back to health by medics. In time, he was picked up and eventually taken to a Prisoner-of-War camp at Featherston, near Wellington, in New Zealand, where he was to spend the next three years, as Don Stephens records in his inspirational book War and Grace (Evangelical Press, an imprint of 10Publishing). Shinya and his fellow inmates were treated with much kindness (in sharp contrast to the torture often experienced by Allied prisoners at the hands of the Japanese). Being showered with gifts at Christmas, a feast he knew nothing about, seemed especially strange. However, he was determined not to be ‘taken in’ by the Christian teaching offered after some of the prisoners requested spiritual help and a Japanese Bible was made available. That is until he chanced upon an article entitled ‘Sorrow in Victory’ in which the author quoted a ‘Hebrew prophet’ as saying: “Those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength. They shall soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary; they will walk and not be faint.” It made a deep impression on him, and he was determined to find out where it came from. Assuming it was from the Old Testament, he began reading the Bible, starting at Genesis chapter 1. Eventually, to his joy, he discovered that the profound words were from the Book of the prophet Isaiah (chapter 40, verse 31). After flagging somewhat in his search, he found himself hospitalised with malaria when a friend brought him a booklet called The Reason Why explaining the way to salvation. It so happened that the camp’s chaplain, Pastor Hessell Troughton, had been a missionary to Japan and spoke the language. Shinya joined others in his Bible studies and came to know and love Jesus as his Saviour. So much did this “complete freedom” now rule his life that prison had morphed into what he described as “a unique paradise on earth”. He never looked back after that and became convinced that his post-war calling would be in service of his Lord. When he finally returned home, his family were shocked to see him alive for he had been reported as killed in action. He had also given a false name to his captors because of the supposed shame of falling into enemy hands. Shinya subsequently became a pastor and prolific writer and translator following years of theological study both in Tokyo and the US. The Old Testament, he came to believe, demonstrated that sin is “the ultimate problem of mankind” and clearly pointed to Christ as the answer. On seeking to understand why so few Japanese became Christians, he felt it was partly due to their pride borne of believing they were a superior race. As for those three Christmases he spent in New Zealand, author Don Stephens writes: “Of all the gifts he received, the one he valued most was ‘the boundless and deep grace and peace of God in the Lord Jesus Christ’.” The post WWII Japanese POW found ‘freedom’ in camp first appeared on God Reports .
content_zh:
查尔斯·加德纳编著: 当一艘日本水手的驱逐舰在二战南太平洋战役中被美国人击沉时,大部分同伴溺毙. 令人惊奇的是,尽管随着船只的下沉,他与其他人一起被吸在海浪下,但鱼雷军官Michiharu Shinya却不知何故幸免于1942年的灾难。 (200人的船员中只有18人这样做).

但他宁愿死在那个时候,因为他的族人被灌输相信被俘虏是可耻的. 然而,他受了重伤,但被医护人员喂养。

在时间上,他被接了起来,最终被带到新西兰惠灵顿附近的费瑟斯顿(Featherston)的战俘营,在那里他将度过接下来的三年,正如唐·斯蒂芬斯在他的励志书"战争与格蕾丝"(福音出版社,10Publishing的印记)中记载的那样.

信也和同狱囚犯受到很大程度的善待(与盟军囚犯经常在日本人手中遭受的酷刑形成鲜明对比). 在圣诞节用礼物淋浴 一个他一无所知的宴会 看起来特别奇怪

然而,在一些囚犯要求精神帮助和提供日本圣经后,他决心不再接受基督教教义的 " 接纳 " 。 直到他看到一篇题为“为胜利而悲伤”的文章,作者在文章中引用了一位“赫布鲁先知”的话:“那些希望主复活的人。 他们将像鹰一样飞翔,

他们将奔驰,而不会疲倦,他们将走路,而不会晕倒。 这给他留下了深刻的印象,他下定决心要找出它来自何处. 假设它来自旧约,他开始阅读圣经,从创世纪第一章开始. 最终,在他的喜悦中,他发现深刻的文字来自先知以赛亚的经典(第40章第31节).

在搜索中略微浮出水面后,他发现自己患上了疟疾,一位朋友给他带了一本小册子,名为《原因》,解释救世之路。 难民营的牧师Hessell Troughton牧师曾是日本的传教士, 信也加入了其他人的圣经研究,来到了了解和热爱耶稣作为他的救世主.

这种“完全自由”现在统治了他的生活,监狱变成了他所称的“地球上独一无二的天堂”。 他从此之后再也没有回头看,并且确信他的战后召唤将会为他的主服务. 当他最终回家时,家人震惊地看到他活着,因为他被报道为阵亡.

他还给抓捕者取了一个假名,因为被假定是落入敌人手中的耻辱。 在东京和美国多年的神学研究之后,信也后来成为一名牧师和多产作家和翻译。 他逐渐相信,《旧约》表明了罪恶是“人类的最终问题”,并明确指出基督是答案。

在试图理解为什么如此少的日本人成为基督徒时,他感到部分是由于他们的自豪感,因为他们相信他们是优越的种族。

至于他在新西兰度过的三个圣诞节,作者Don Stephens写道:"在他收到的所有礼物中,他最珍视的一件是`上帝在耶稣基督中无限和深厚的恩惠与和平 ' 。 日本战俘在营地发现「自由」,

title_zh: 在西部明星的阴影下：格罗弗·刘易斯、拉里·麦克默特里和文字的胜利
content: With The Grover Lewis Reader: Splendor in the Short Grass and Western Star , the newest biography of Larry McMurtry, in hand, I load my truck and head toward Archer City, Texas, accompanied by my wife, Melanie, and our friend Eliott. Archer City is, of course, McMurtry country, a small Texas town made famous through the literary imagination of one of America’s most celebrated novelists. Having written about McMurtry’s faith—or lack thereof—in a previous article , following an earlier visit to Archer City, I’m returning with a somewhat different interest. This time, my attention turns to Grover Lewis, the gifted journalist, critic, and poet whose life intersected with McMurtry’s during their college years. Lewis’ story, however, begins not with literary achievement but with almost unimaginable tragedy. As a child, he experienced the devastating loss of both parents when his father murdered his mother and was subsequently shot with the same gun, either by his dying wife or another person present. Lewis was only eight years old. It is difficult to imagine a more horrific beginning. Yet rather than allowing that tragedy to become the entirety of his story, Lewis eventually found a voice through literature. Perhaps the cards life dealt him gave him plenty to write about. Or perhaps writing became his way of making sense of a world that had revealed its cruelty far too early. In his autobiographical poem “Hillbilly Song,” Lewis writes: “You asked me once, Ann/Over coffee gone cold with talk/In your mother’s rain-drowsy/House, who they were, how it/Was with them in their breathless/Time in the wilds of years.” For Lewis, those early years were indeed wild. But they were also the soil from which his literary imagination would eventually grow. A Life in Words Born in Texas in 1934, Grover Lewis emerged as a distinctive voice in American journalism, particularly through his cultural criticism and reporting on the rapidly changing landscape of the 1960s and 1970s. He became known for his sharp observations, literary flair, and ability to capture the personalities and contradictions of American culture, even if he occasionally stretched the truth in the telling. His work appeared in prominent publications, including Rolling Stone , where his reporting helped establish his reputation as an insightful, sometimes cutting observer of popular culture. Lewis was more than a journalist, however. He was a poet and literary craftsman, someone who understood that words could do more than convey information. They could illuminate the human condition, expose its contradictions, and perhaps even provide a measure of healing. Grover Lewis (ChatPGT) Continuing “Hillbilly Song,” Lewis ponders: “At last, breathless and dry-mouthed/With private desire in the blue,/Swollen dark, we all lie down together—/My mother, my father, their perishing/Dreams, and I this unborn prisoner son…” There is something haunting about these lines. The dead remain present. The past refuses to disappear. And the poet, even as an adult, seems to wrestle with the circumstances that shaped his entrance into the world. Yet the very act of writing suggests something else: a refusal to remain silent. Two Texans, Two Literary Paths Lewis and Larry McMurtry crossed paths as students at North Texas State College, now the University of North Texas, during the 1950s. Both were young Texans drawn to literature and the possibilities of the written word. Their friendship developed within a shared intellectual environment, one that encouraged reading, conversation, and the pursuit of literary ambitions. Although their careers eventually followed different paths—McMurtry toward novels, screenplays, and literary fame, Lewis toward journalism, poetry, and cultural criticism—they shared an interest in the complexities of American life. content_zh:
与《格罗弗·刘易斯读者:短草中的辉煌与西部之星》,拉里·麦克默特里的最新传记, 手持,我装载我的卡车并前往德克萨斯州阿彻城, 由我的妻子梅兰妮和我们的朋友埃利奥特陪同。 阿彻城当然是麦克默特里国家,一个通过美国最著名的小说家之一的文学想象而成名的德克萨斯小镇.

在之前访问Archer城后, 我对McMurtry的信仰(或缺乏信仰)有一番兴趣, 这一次,我转而关注有天赋的记者、评论家和诗人格罗弗·刘易斯,他在大学时代的生活与麦克默特里的生活交织在一起。

然而,刘易斯的故事并非从文学成就开始,而是从几乎难以想象的悲剧开始. 他从小就经历了父母的惨痛损失,当时他的父亲谋杀了他的母亲,随后被他即将死亡的妻子或在场的其他人用同一把枪射杀。 刘易斯才八岁 很难想象一个更可怕的开端。

然而,刘易斯最终没有让这场悲剧成为他的全部故事,而是通过文学找到了声音. 也许他命中注定的卡片 给他写了很多东西 或写作成为他理解世界的方式, 这个世界已经揭示了它的残酷性,还为时过早。

刘易斯在自传诗“Hillbilly Song”中写道 : “ 你曾经问过我,Ann/Over咖啡随着谈话而变得冷淡,在你妈妈的雨滴/住所里,他们是谁,他们在无气息的年代/在野外时如何。 ” 对刘易斯来说,那些早年的确很狂野. 但它们也是他的文学想象最终会成长的土壤.

1934年出生于德克萨斯州的"言语生活"(A Life in Words Born in Texas),格罗弗·刘易斯(Grover Lewis)成为美国新闻业中一个有特色的代言人,特别是通过他对1960年代和1970年代迅速变化的地貌的文化批评和报道.

他以尖锐的观察,文学的才华,以及能够捕捉美国文化的个性和矛盾而闻名,即使他偶尔在讲述中伸张真理. 他的作品出现在包括滚石公司在内的著名出版物中,他的报道帮助他树立了自己作为有见地,有时剪切流行文化观察者的声誉.

然而,刘易斯不只是一名记者。 他是一位诗人和文学家,一个懂得文字可以比传递信息更有用的人. 它们可以揭示人类的状况,暴露其矛盾,甚至可能提供某种治疗方法。

Grover Lewis (ChatPGT) 继续“Hillbilly Song,” 刘易斯思考道:“最后,无气息和干燥的嘴唇/在蓝色的暗处私欲下,我们都躺在一起——/我的母亲、父亲、他们的死亡/梦想,我这个未出生的囚犯儿子......” 这些台词有些困扰。 死者仍然在场。 过去拒绝消失。

而诗人,即使作为一个成年人,似乎也与塑造他进入世界的环境相搏. 然而,写作本身就暗示了另一种情况:拒绝保持沉默。 两德克萨斯州立大学,两条文学道路刘易斯州立大学和拉里·麦克默特里(英语:Larry McMurtry)在1950年代作为北德克萨斯州立学院,即现在的北德克萨斯大学的学生跨过道路.

两人都是年轻的德克萨斯人,被吸引到文学和写字的可能性. 他们的友谊是在共同的知识环境中发展起来的,这种环境鼓励阅读,对话,追求文学野心.

尽管他们的职业生涯最终走的是不同的道路——小说、剧本和文学名人、刘易斯新闻、诗歌和文化批评——但他们对美国生活的复杂性有着共同的兴趣。 麦克默特里和刘易斯在大学期间(ChatGPT)都拥有超越德克萨斯州和美国西部神话的能力,认识到孤独,凝视

summary_zh: 文：查尔斯·加德纳（Charles Gardner）——一位犹太籍陆军外科医生对一名年轻士兵的勇气感到惊叹，这名士兵在美国内战（1861-65）的葛底斯堡战役中身受重伤。为了挽救这个男孩的生命，马克斯·罗斯瓦利（Max Rossvally）博士不得不截肢，截掉了他的一条腿和一条胳膊。但这改变了他自己……  这篇题为《犹太军医在目睹病人的勇气后归向耶稣》的文章  最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
title_zh: 犹太军医在目睹病人的勇气后归信耶稣
content: Pastor Peter Colon portraying Major Rossvally in the movie of his story By Charles Gardner — A Jewish army surgeon was amazed by the courage of a young soldier badly wounded in the Battle of Gettysburg during the American Civil War (1861-65). Dr Max Rossvally was forced to amputate both a leg and arm in a bid to save the boy’s life. But it changed his own life. For the 17-year-old Drummer Boy – too young for frontline duty – refused chloroform or brandy to dull the pain. Charlie Coulson chose instead to trust in Jesus, his Lord and Saviour. The doctor – an army major and Orthodox Jew – was understandably stunned by the boy’s bravery, as well as his boldness in declaring his faith in Christ and imploring the officer (whom he knew to be Jewish) to put his own trust in Jesus, since he was also the Jewish Messiah. Max, however, was shaken rigid, and in a great dilemma, as he had always been taught to hate Jesus. For his people had largely rejected him as an ‘impostor’ and false Messiah. Charlie died just days later, apparently more concerned for the doctor’s eternal destiny than for his own painful exit from this life. Ten years later, Max found himself in a barber’s chair in New York once more being urged to trust in Jesus. Having explained the gospel, the barber promised to pray for him and said that, whenever he came in contact with a Jew, he felt it his duty to introduce him to the one who came for “the lost sheep of Israel” (Matthew 10:6). The surgeon subsequently boarded a train for a business meeting in Washington, where a newspaper advertisement drew him to a ‘revival’ service where the preacher echoed the messages he had heard from the barber and the boy soldier, leaving him in tears. He agonised at home in prayer for some time afterwards, struggling most of all with the thought that, if he accepted Christ, he would be going against all the advice and teaching he had known, not to mention the Jewish community as a whole. But he finally became convinced that Jesus was indeed the fulfilment of Old Testament prophecies (in particular, Genesis 49:10, Micah 5:2 and Isaiah 7:14). So he prayed: “O Lord God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. You know I am sincere in this thing. If Jesus Christ is the Son of God, reveal him to me this night, and I will accept him as my Messiah.” A long battle ensued, but his doubts were eventually replaced by joy and happiness as he praised God that he had found the true Shiloh, Ruler of Israel and Emmanuel. He was to pay a high price, however, as do all who follow Christ. His wife walked out on him; his parents disowned him. But he never gave up hope as he constantly prayed and reached out to his family. After 54 days, his wife joined him as a disciple of Jesus and, in time, his daughter also became a believer. But his son disowned him for many years until he was eventually reconciled both with his earthly and heavenly Father. In an extraordinary sequel some 18 months after he came to Christ, Max met up with Mrs Coulson, the mother of his dying young patient all those years earlier on the battlefield. With great joy, he was able to share how her son had set him on the path to a glorious future in Christ, which was to touch lives across the world, including my home county of Yorkshire in England. In fact, he came to live in Leeds to reach out to the Jewish community there and is buried at Lawnswood Cemetery in the city. An Irish friend of mine, Colin Nevin, has visited the grave, which includes an excerpt from one of the doctor’s hymns, I am Coming Soon, and was able to give a copy of Max’s story to a caretaker, so continuing the evangelist’s legacy more than a century after his death in 1892, aged 64. A 54-minute movie – Rossvally: From the Synagogue to the Saviour – has been produced on DVD and can apparently be ordered online. The post Jewish army doctor turned to Jesus after witnessing patient’s courage first appeared on God Reports .
content_zh:
牧师彼得·科隆在他的故事电影"查尔斯·加德纳"(By Charles Gardner)中描绘了罗斯瓦利少校——一位犹太军队外科医生对美国内战期间格底斯堡战役(1861-65)中一名年轻士兵严重受伤的勇气感到惊讶. Max Rossvally医生被迫截肢, 但这改变了他自己的生活。

对于17岁的Drummer Boy — — 年龄太小,无法承担前线任务 — — 拒绝氯仿或白兰地来消磨疼痛。 查理·科尔森选择了信任耶稣,他的主和救世主.

这位医生是一名陆军少校和正统犹太人,对男孩的勇敢以及他大胆地宣布对基督的信仰,恳求军官(他知道是犹太人)相信耶稣是可以理解的,因为他也是犹太弥赛亚。 然而,马克思被动摇僵硬,陷入了巨大的困境,因为他一直被教导要憎恨耶稣.

他的宗族曾否认他是一个 " 骗子 " 和假的弥赛亚。 Charlie在几天后就去世了,显然更关心医生的永恒命运,而不是他自己痛苦地离开这一生。 10年后,马克思发现自己在纽约的理发师座椅上再次被敦促信任耶稣.

在解释了福音之后,理发师答应为他祈祷,并说每当他与一个犹太人接触时,他觉得有义务将他介绍给前来寻找“迷失的以色列羊”的人(Matthew 10:6)。

外科医生随后登上火车在华盛顿举行商务会议,报纸的广告将他引向 " 复活 " 服务,传教士重复了他从理发师和男孩士兵那里听到的信息,使他流泪。

他在家里苦苦地祈祷了一段时间,他首先想到,如果他接受基督,他将反对他所知道的所有建议和教导,更不用说整个犹太社区了。 但他最终确信耶稣确实是"旧约预言"的实现(特别是创世纪49:10,米迦5:2和以赛亚7:14).

他就祈祷说:易卜拉欣、易司哈格、叶尔孤白的主啊! 你知道我对这件事很真诚 如果耶稣基督是上帝之子,那么今晚把他告诉我,我将接受他为我的弥赛亚。” 一场漫长的战斗随之而来,但他的疑虑最终被欢乐和幸福所取代,因为他称赞上帝找到了真正的希洛,以色列统治者和埃马纽埃尔.

但他要付出高昂的代价,跟随基督的所有人一样。 他的妻子抛弃了他;他的父母抛弃了他。 但是,他从未放弃过希望,因为他不断祈祷和联系家人。 在54天后,他的妻子作为耶稣的门徒加入了他,在时间上,他的女儿也成为了信徒.

但他的儿子与他断绝关系多年,直到他最终与他的大地父和天父都和解. 在他来到基督的大约18个月之后的一段非凡续集中,马克思在战场上遇见了那些年前他死去的年轻病人的母亲科尔森夫人.

他怀着极大的喜悦,得以分享她儿子如何使他踏上基督辉煌未来的道路,这就是触摸世界各地的生活,包括我的家乡英格兰约克郡. 事实上,他来到利兹居住,向那里的犹太社区伸出援手,并被埋在城内的草坪林墓地.

我的一个爱尔兰朋友科林·内文参观了这个坟墓,其中包括医生颂歌"I am Coming Soon"的节录,并且能够把马克思的故事复制给看守人,因此在1892年去世后一个多世纪的福音派传承下来,享年64岁.

一部54分钟的电影 — — Rossvally: 从Synagogue到救世主 — 已经在DVD上制作,显然可以在网上订购. 在目睹病人的勇气首次出现在上帝的报告之后,

God mercifully saved me during the Jesus Revolution (1970), out of a hippie lifestyle and a passionate, though misguided pursuit of truth through far eastern religious practices (yoga and meditation). Shortly after encountering […]  The post  Two truck tires and a white dove taught me to trust God  first appeared on  God Reports .
summary_zh:
由迈克·史瑞夫(Mike Shreve)——福音主义一直是我55年来的焦点,在全美国和其他14个国家担任部长. 上帝在耶稣革命期间(1970年)从嬉皮的生活方式和热情中怜悯地拯救了我,尽管通过远东宗教实践(瑜伽和冥想)错误地追求真理.

碰面后不久... 两辆卡车轮胎和一只白鸽教我相信上帝,
title_zh: 两只卡车轮胎和一只白鸽教会了我信靠上帝
content: By Mike Shreve — Tent meeting in the 80s Evangelism has been my focus for 55 years, ministering throughout the United States and in 14 other nations. God mercifully saved me during the Jesus Revolution (1970), out of a hippie lifestyle and a passionate, though misguided pursuit of truth through far eastern religious practices (yoga and meditation). Shortly after encountering Jesus and being delivered, along with another brother in the Lord, I began hitchhiking around the country, preaching the Gospel on street corners and college campuses. That developed through the years into ministry in churches, auditoriums, conferences, and tent crusades. Supernatural provision and divine intervention has always carried me, through every phase of this five-and-a-half-decade-long adventure. However, the following story is a classic. For about 25 years I carried big Gospel tents around the country. At the time of this “miracle,” I was transporting a 60’ x 90’ tent from one city to the next in an old, dilapidated bus that kept introducing new challenges to our amateur mechanic skills (putting it mildly). One day, on our way to Tampa, Florida—unfortunately—we hit a large pothole in the road that put a serious dent in the rear left rim on which a large truck tire was mounted. From that point, the inner tube would not retain air, making it necessary to stop every thirty miles or so to fill it up again . . . and again . . . and again . . . making the trip painfully slow. Adding to the problem, the other rear tire was bald, and we had no spare (couldn’t afford one). So, a flat would have brought us to a complete standstill. Sometimes, I think back on those days (when our zeal for the Kingdom outran any wisdom we might have possessed), and I marvel at the many times God took care of us anyway (like the loving heavenly Father that He is). Thousands of pounds of equipment were packed into that groaning, creaking, rusty, decrepit bus — heavy canvas tent sections, metal poles, stakes, platform, and 300 chairs—and only a few days allowed in between cities for transit and setup. No, we really could not afford any setbacks. And yes, a lot of “faith prayers” were uttered during every trip (or were they “presumptive proclamations”—not sure—maybe a mix of the two). An old split rim tire mounted on an old bus Once we got to Tampa, attempting to be frugal, I visited the junkyards hoping to find a used replacement rim. As if they had conspired to dissuade me, every junkyard owner/manager shot down my hopes with a similar assessment, “Fella, you won’t find one of them old split-rims anywhere. They’re dangerous. When you try to mount a tire on one, they can snap open and injure somebody real bad, cutting off a hand, even killing a person. We melted ‘em all down as scrap metal.” (Go ahead, look them up online—they were even called “widow-makers.”) It was the same story everywhere I went. Nobody could help. Then three weeks passed and we had to pack the bus and head to our next location—Bessemer City, North Carolina. It was a college-level, biblically-sound course on developing long-suffering and patience: stopping every thirty miles or so to air up that unpredictable tire, pleading with God to somehow supernaturally assist us in our journey by making sure none of the tires blew. Somehow, we made it—around 600 miles—stopping about 25 times. Then an incredible miracle happened! God did it and I still feel awestruck, just writing about it. As we turned into the fairgrounds area, right in the middle of the entrance were two brand new, neatly-stacked truck tires (unclaimed), exactly the size we used on the bus—mounted (you guessed it!) on the very same split rims our bus required. Talk about worshiping God—we launched into a praise session right then and there! What were the odds? We all knew it had to be God. Jehovah-Jireh (the Lord our provider) had fulfilled His amazing promise to do “exceedingly, abundantly above all” we could ask or think (Ephesians 3:20). Then li
content_zh:
麦克史瑞夫 80年代的帐篷会议是我55年来的焦点,在美国和14个其他国家担任部长。 上帝在耶稣革命期间(1970年)从嬉皮的生活方式和热情中怜悯地拯救了我,尽管通过远东宗教实践(瑜伽和冥想)错误地追求真理.

在遇到耶稣和被送走后不久,我与上帝的另一个兄弟一起,开始搭便车到全国各地,在街角和大学校园传福音. 多年来,这在教堂、礼堂、会议和帐篷十字军中发展成部。

超自然的供给和神的干预 总是让我在五年半的历险历程中 然而,以下的故事是一个经典的故事. 大约25年来,我在全国各地搭载着大型福音帐篷。

在这个“奇迹”发生时,我正用一辆老旧、破旧的公交车将60×90的帐篷从一个城市运送到另一个城市,这辆公交车不断给我们的业余技工技能带来新的挑战(轻轻地推开)。 有一天,在前往佛罗里达州坦帕的路上——不幸地——我们撞上了路边的一个大坑洞,在后左侧竖起一个大型卡车轮胎,后侧有严重的凹痕。

从此,内管不会保留空气,使得每30英里左右必须停一次才能再次填充. . . 再加上问题, 另一台后轮胎是秃头, 因此,一个公寓会 使我们完全停顿。

有时,我想起那些时候(那时我们对王国的热情超越了我们可能拥有的任何智慧),我惊讶地看到,无论怎样,上帝总是照顾我们(就像他那慈爱的天父)。

数千磅的设备被装进那辆呻吟、颤抖、生锈、破烂的巴士——重型帆布帐篷路段、金属杆、木桩、平台和300张椅子——而且只有几天时间允许在城市之间过境和布置。 不,我们真的无法承受任何挫折。

在每次旅行中都发表了许多“信仰祷告”(或它们是否“假定的宣告”——不确定——可能是两者的混合)。 一辆旧公共汽车上挂着一个旧的分叉轮圈轮胎 一旦我们到了坦帕, 试图节俭, 我参观了垃圾场 希望找到一个旧的替代轮圈。

就像他们密谋劝阻我一样, 每个垃圾场老板/经理都用类似的评估来击落我的希望, “伙计, 他们很危险。 当你试图安装一个轮胎, 他们可以撕开和伤害一个人 真正的坏,切断一只手,甚至杀死一个人。

我们把它们都融化成废金属。” 他们甚至被称为“寡妇制造者”。 我去过的地方都一样 没人能帮上忙 然后三个星期过去了,我们不得不收拾公交车 并前往下一个地点——北卡罗莱纳州的贝瑟默市。

这是一个关于发展长期痛苦和耐心的大学级、圣经般的教程:每隔30英里左右就停下来吹吹那个不可预测的轮胎,恳求上帝以某种超自然的方式协助我们的旅程,确保没有轮胎爆炸。 不知何故,我们大约在600英里的距离里,停了25次。 奇迹发生了!

上帝做到了,我仍然感觉 西车,只是写它。 当我们变成广场时, 就在入口的中间, 两个全新的, 整洁的卡车轮胎(无人认领), 说到崇拜上帝——我们发起了一次赞美会议,

什么机会? 我们都知道那是真主。耶和华已满足了。 他令人惊奇地承诺“超越一切, 然后说

title: Rejoice in the Lamb: Benjamin Britten, Christopher Smart, and the Poetry of Faith
summary: When music meets poetry, the result can be more than art, it can become an expression of spiritual wonder. The last time I heard Professor Bruce Redford speak about the eccentric British clergyman and poet Christopher Smart (1722–1771), I was so inspired that I included a substantial portion of Smart’s extraordinary poem, Jubilate Agno, in […]  The post  Rejoice in the Lamb: Benjamin Britten, Christopher Smart, and the Poetry of Faith  first appeared on  God Reports .
summary_zh:
当音乐与诗歌相遇时,结果可以超越艺术,成为精神奇迹的体现.

上次我听到布鲁斯·雷德福德教授 谈到古怪的英国神职人员和诗人克里斯托弗·斯马特(1722–1771)时,我受到很大启发,在[.]中包含了一大部分斯马特非凡的诗歌,大庆阿格诺. 以及《信仰之诗》,
title_zh: 喜悦羔羊：本杰明·布里顿、克里斯托弗·斯马特和信仰的诗歌
content: When music meets poetry, the result can be more than art, it can become an expression of spiritual wonder. Christopher Smart The last time I heard Professor Bruce Redford speak about the eccentric British clergyman and poet Christopher Smart (1722–1771), I was so inspired that I included a substantial portion of Smart’s extraordinary poem, Jubilate Agno , in my book Beauty (And the Banana) . I described Smart as a theopoet , someone whose deep religious convictions found expression through a distinctive and imaginative poetic vision. Smart was no ordinary poet. His writings moved freely between the sacred and the seemingly mundane, finding divine significance in everything from biblical figures to animals and the natural world. His poetry was exuberant, unconventional, and, at times, wonderfully strange. For Smart, creation itself was a chorus of praise, and every living thing had a part to play. Recently, I had another opportunity to hear Redford explore Smart’s remarkable literary legacy, this time through the music of British composer Benjamin Britten (1913–1976). As part of an All Saints’ Day concert at the Cathedral of St. John in Albuquerque, New Mexico, celebrating Britten’s music, Redford delivered a pre-concert lecture focusing on the composer’s Rejoice in the Lamb , a choral masterpiece that brings Smart’s unusual poetry to life. The evening offered a fascinating intersection of literature, music, theology, and history, demonstrating how two artists separated by nearly two centuries could share a common vision of wonder. The Musical Imagination of Benjamin Britten Benjamin Britten. Photo: Public Domain. Redford, a former professor at Boston University who was living in England when Britten died in 1976, identified three defining characteristics of the composer’s work. First, Britten’s music is distinguished by “passion and variety.” His compositions resist easy categorization, moving between emotional intensity, dramatic storytelling, and moments of remarkable spiritual intimacy. Redford described Britten’s approach as creating a kind of musical parable, pointing to Curlew River , one of Britten’s church parables, as a particularly compelling example. Second, Britten demonstrated an extraordinary ability to balance “economy and scope.” Redford compared this quality to the novels of Jane Austen, whose carefully constructed narratives reveal entire worlds through seemingly modest details. Similarly, Britten could communicate profound emotional and spiritual truths through restrained musical means. Nothing was wasted; every note served a purpose. Third, and perhaps most important for the evening’s performance, Britten possessed an exceptional “sensitivity to words.” Redford described him as an “inspired” interpreter of literary texts, a composer who understood that music should not merely accompany poetry but illuminate its deeper meaning. It was this third characteristic that led Redford to Christopher Smart. When an Eccentric Poet Meets a Brilliant Composer In 1943, Britten composed Rejoice in the Lamb (Op. 30), a festival cantata scored for four soloists, SATB choir, and organ. The composition draws its text from Smart’s Jubilate Agno , a work of religious poetry that remained largely unknown for nearly two centuries. Christopher Smart Smart wrote much of the poem during his confinement in a private madhouse in eighteenth-century London. Its unconventional structure, biblical references, exuberant language, and seemingly spontaneous declarations of praise made it unlike almost anything else in English religious literature. The manuscript remained unpublished until W. F. Stead brought it to public attention in 1939. Soon afterward, the poet W. H. Auden introduced Britten to Smart’s newly published work while the composer was living in the United States. The connection proved fruitful. Britten recognized something remarkable in Smart’s poetry: an unrestrained celebration of creation that could be translated into music.
content_zh:
当音乐与诗歌相遇时,结果可以超越艺术,成为精神奇迹的体现. 克里斯托弗·聪明 上次我听到布鲁斯·雷德福德教授谈到古怪的英国神职人员和诗人克里斯托弗·斯马特(1722–1771)时,我深受启发,在我的书《美人(和香蕉)》中包含了一大部分斯马特非凡的诗集《阿格诺大庆》。

我形容Smart是一位戏剧家, 聪明不是普通诗人 他的著作在圣人和看似庸俗的人之间自由移动,在从圣经人物到动物和自然世界的一切事物中都发现了神圣的意义.

他的诗歌充满了活力,与众不同,有时也非常奇怪. 对于Smart来说,创作本身是赞美的合唱,每一个活物都有角色可以扮演. 最近,我又有机会听到雷德福德探索Smart杰出的文学遗产,这次是通过英国作曲家本杰明·布里顿的音乐(1913–1976).

作为新墨西哥州阿尔布开克圣约翰大教堂庆祝布列顿音乐的全圣人节音乐会的一部分,雷德福德发表了一场音乐会前演讲,重点讲述了作曲家在羊羔中的欢乐,这是一部将斯马特不寻常的诗歌带给人生的奇特杰作.

晚上提供了文学、音乐、神学和历史的奇妙交汇点,展示了两个艺术家如何在将近两个世纪的时间里分开,可以分享一个共同的奇观。 本杰明·布林顿·本杰明·布林顿的音乐想象. 图片:公共域名.

雷德福德(Redford)是波士顿大学前教授,1976年布里顿逝世时居住在英国,他确定了作曲家作品的三个决定性特征. 首先,布列顿的音乐以“热情和多样性”来区分。 他的构思抵制轻松的分类,在情感的强度,戏剧性的故事性,以及非凡的精神亲密的时刻之间移动.

Redford将布列顿的做法描述为创造了一种音乐比喻,指向了布列顿教堂比喻之一的Curlew River,作为特别有说服力的例子.

第二,Britten表现出了平衡“经济和范围”的非凡能力。 雷德福德将这种品质与简·奥斯汀的小说相比较,他精心构建的叙事通过看似微小的细节揭示了整个世界. 同样,布列顿可以通过受约束的音乐手段传达深刻的情感和精神真理. 没有浪费任何东西;每张纸条都有作用。

第三,或许对晚间演出来说最重要的,布列顿拥有一种非凡的“言语敏感性 ” 。 Redford将他描述为文学文本的“受启发的”解释者,他是一个作曲家,他明白音乐不应仅仅伴随着诗歌,而应阐明其更深层次的意义。 正是这第三个特征导致雷德福找到克里斯托弗·斯马特.

1943年,当一位爱心诗人遇到一位杰出的作曲家时,布列顿在"羔羊"(Op. 30)中编曲了"欢乐"(Rejoice in the Lamb (Op. 30)),一个节日的Cantata为四位独奏家,SATB合唱团和管风琴打分. 内容来自Smart's Jubilate Agno, 一部宗教诗歌作品,

克里斯托弗·斯马特(Christopher Smart Smart)在18世纪伦敦一个私人疯人院禁闭期间写下了这首诗的大部分内容. 它的非常规结构,圣经的参考文献,兴旺的语言,以及看似自发的赞美宣言,使得它几乎不同于英国宗教文献中的其他任何内容. 手稿直到W. F.

施泰德在1939年引起了公众的注意. 不久之后,诗人W·H·奥登(W. H. Auden)在作曲家在美国居住期间,向布里顿介绍了斯马特新出版的作品. 这种联系证明是富有成果的。 Britten在Smart的诗歌中承认了一些令人瞩目的事物:一种可以被翻译成音乐的无限制的创作庆典.
author: Brian Nixon

title: Jewish refugee became vicar
summary: By Charles Gardner — At a time when Hitler aimed to harm us, here was a German who came to bless us! Holocaust survivor Werner Simonson escaped from Germany just before the outbreak of World War II, only to become a Church of England vicar. Of Jewish heritage, he was sacked as a judge by […]  The post  Jewish refugee became vicar  first appeared on  God Reports .
summary_zh: 文：查尔斯·加德纳（Charles Gardner）——在希特勒企图迫害我们的时期，这位德国人却来祝福我们！大屠杀幸存者维尔纳·西蒙森（Werner Simonson）在第二次世界大战爆发前夕逃离德国，后来成为英国国教的牧师。他有犹太血统，被……解除了法官职务。这篇题为《犹太难民成为牧师》的文章最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
title_zh: 犹太难民成为副牧师
content: Werner Simonson By Charles Gardner — At a time when Hitler aimed to harm us, here was a German who came to bless us! Holocaust survivor Werner Simonson escaped from Germany just before the outbreak of World War II, only to become a Church of England vicar. Of Jewish heritage, he was sacked as a judge by the Nazis and had to endure long years of separation from his non-Jewish wife and son before being reunited after the war. Like John Wesley who was rescued as a child from a rectory fire, Werner was also ‘a brand plucked from the burning’. He was about to be executed in a World War I battle with France when he and his colleagues were wrongly accused of shooting French prisoners. But just in time, one of the latter told the firing squad how Werner had treated him with kindness, even sharing his rations with him. The German soldier was thus spared but spent the next five years as a prisoner of the French, his POW status only ending in 1920 after being put to work restoring war damage in northern France. When finally released, it was a case of ‘from the frying pan into the fire’ as Germany was plunged into despair and division following their ignominious defeat. Despite this, however, Werner quickly rose to the status of high court judge before being dismissed from his post by the Nazis when they discovered his Jewish heritage. The fact that he had fought for Germany and had won the coveted Iron Cross for gallantry counted for nothing. And the increasing pressure of anticipating arrest led to a breakdown of his health. But while attending his niece’s confirmation at a Lutheran church, feeling at the end of his rope, it was as if the preacher was speaking directly into his desperate situation. He opened his heart to Christ and found new life and hope. “In the utter darkness which had engulfed my life I saw a new light,” he recalled.(1) He became associated with the Confessing Church opposing the Nazis’ antisemitic policies and was advised to escape which he managed to do with the help of the Bishop of Chichester Dr George Bell. Werner’s wife Leonie and son Juergen stayed behind but were able to join him after the war. Being German, he was initially interned with others on the Isle of Man where he led fellow Jews to faith in Christ. But tragic news followed, hearing of his father’s death, his mother being murdered in a concentration camp and his sister Ilse gassed in Auschwitz. Werner knew little English when he arrived on these shores but attracted much interest by being ordained at St Paul’s Cathedral when Britain was in the middle of a war with his fatherland. He was subsequently offered back the post of judge in the new West Germany along with a pension for the job from which he had been previously dismissed by the Nazis. But he turned down the generous offer. “I could not exchange service in the ministry of God for service in administering man-made law; accepting this offer would have meant abandoning God’s call to me, and this I could not do.” But this humble and self-effacing man was to make a significant impact in succeeding years as he proclaimed the gospel in three separate London parishes, ending up at St Luke’s, Hampstead, where (from 1956-1965) he helped yet more Jewish people to a knowledge of their Messiah. He continued passionately preaching Christ almost till his final breath in 1991, aged 101. 1 With grateful thanks to War and Grace by Don Stephens (Evangelical Press 2005), an imprint of 10Publishing. The post Jewish refugee became vicar first appeared on God Reports .
content_zh:
维纳·西蒙森 查尔斯·加德纳 当希特勒想伤害我们的时候 有个德国人来祝福我们! 大屠杀幸存者维尔纳·西蒙森(Werner Simonson)在二战爆发前刚从德国逃出,只是成为英国牧师教堂.

由于犹太人的遗产,他被纳粹解雇为法官,不得不忍受与他非犹太妻子和儿子多年的分离,战争结束后才重新团聚. 就像小时候被救出来的约翰·卫斯理(John Wesley),

他在第一次世界大战与法国的战斗中即将被处决,当时他和他的同事被错误地指责射杀法国囚犯. 但就在时间上,后者之一告诉行刑队,沃纳如何以善意对待他,甚至与他分享他的口粮.

德国士兵因此幸免于难,但作为法国人的俘虏度过了接下来的五年,他的战俘身份直到1920年在法国北部被投入恢复战争破坏后才结束. 当德国在惨败之后陷入绝望和分裂。

尽管如此,维尔纳在发现他的犹太遗产后很快升格为高等法院法官,然后被纳粹解职. 他为德国而战 赢得了贪婪的铁十字勋章 他的英勇无足轻重 而预期被捕的压力越来越大,导致他的健康崩溃。

但当在路德会教堂出席侄女的确认仪式时,感觉他的绳索尽头,就像传教士直接谈到他的绝望处境一样. 他向基督敞开了心扉,找到了新的生命和希望.

" 在席卷我的生活的完全黑暗中,我看到了新的光芒, " 他回忆说。 (1) 他与反对纳粹反帝政策的忏悔教会有关联,并被劝告在奇切斯特主教乔治·贝尔博士的帮助下逃离。 维尔纳的妻子莱昂尼(Leonie)和儿子朱尔根(Juergen)留下,但战后得以加入他.

作为德国人,他最初在马恩岛和其他人一起被关押,在那里他带领犹太人同胞信仰基督. 但悲剧性的消息接踵而至,听到他父亲的死讯,他的母亲在集中营被谋杀,他的妹妹伊尔塞在奥斯威辛被毒气冲昏.

Werner在到达这些海岸时不懂英语, 随后他又被重新聘回新西德的法官职位,并同时获得先前被纳粹开除的职务养老金. 但他拒绝了慷慨的提议.

“我不能在上帝部交换服务,以服务于管理人造法律;

接受这个提议将意味着放弃上帝对我的召唤,我不能这样做。 但是,这位谦卑而自卑的人在接下来的岁月里,当他在三个独立的伦敦教区宣布福音时,将产生显著的影响,最后在汉普斯特德的圣卢克(St Luke),他在那里(从1956年到1965年)帮助了更多的犹太人民了解他们的弥赛亚。

他继续热情地宣扬基督,几乎到1991年他最后一口气为止,101. 1岁,感谢战争与恩典,唐·斯蒂芬斯著(福音出版社,2005年),10Publishing的印记. 犹太难民成为牧师,

title_zh: 圣经预言对伊朗战争有何说法？
content: By Mark Ellis – As a 10-year-old boy, Mark Davidson’s mother gave him Hal Lindsey’s book, The Late Great Planet Earth , which eventually sold some 35 million copies, and was declared the bestselling nonfiction book of the 1970s by the New York Times. The book had a great impact on Davidson and shaped his earliest views about end times Bible prophecy. Shaken by the events of 9/11, Davidson, a retired aerospace engineer, dug more deeply into end-times prophecy, seeking answers about the direction of world events.  As he dove into Scripture related to prophecy, he developed a framework that diverges from traditional teaching in several ways, and resulted in his book: Daniel Revisited : Discovering the Four Mideast Signs Leading to the Antichrist. The most relevant of his teaching to current events is his view of Iran. Based on his study of Daniel 7, Daniel 8 and Revelation 6, Davidson identified four major events, which he calls “signposts,” that he believes will unfold in the Middle East before the Tribulation. The four signposts will all be within the Islamic realm. “This interpretation involves the four beasts of Daniel 7, the ram and goat of Daniel 8, and the four horsemen of Revelation 6,” Davidson told God Reports. “They’re all talking about the same four events, just from different aspects.” He says the first signpost was fulfilled when Iraq’s government changed between 2003 and 2005, and he now sees the Iran conflict and disruption involving the Strait of Hormuz as potential indications that the second is beginning to unfold. The second signpost involves Iran (Shia) attacking its Sunni neighbors. “At some point, Iran will destroy the rest of the Arab oil infrastructure of Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the UAE, Qatar, and Iraq,” Davidson predicts, based on his interpretation. “They’ve told the U.S. and Israel, if you attack and destroy our energy infrastructure, we’re going to do the same to all the other neighboring countries.” The attacks could be imminent, based on statements by leaders on both sides. “Iran’s threatening to do this prior to November 3 rd as an October surprise, and Trump is threatening to attack after the midterm elections. “So it could actually be quite soon where it blows up. But that’s what I see happening: the U.S. and Israel would attack Iran. Iran would fend it off like they’ve done before, destroy the rest of the Arab infrastructure, taking oil to astronomical prices.” The economic chaos and disruption could potentially threaten the US’s status as the reserve currency for the world. “Iran is going to take away the peace of mind of the entire earth,” Davidson maintains. “People will wonder how they can put food on the table.” Davidson wrote his book to warn the church because he contends the second signpost is going to be terrible. “It’s going to be awful. It’s going to change all our lives and change how we live, both in the United States as well as in much of the world. Mark Davidson “The second signpost is going to hit us in the face. I was completely aghast and flabbergasted that a U.S. president would trigger the second signpost. I was very, very surprised. “This is a whole Pandora’s box, and once the second signpost happens, that leads to the third, which leads to the fourth, which leads to the Tribulation. So, what God has done is He’s used President Trump to trigger the signpost, to trigger the coming of the Antichrist, to trigger the end of the world, and trigger Christ’s return.” If Davidson was advising President Trump, he would tell him to withdraw US forces as soon as possible. Davidson believes the rebuilding of the Jewish Temple will occur during the third signpost. He diverges from traditional teaching with his view that the coming Antichrist will be a Syrian Arab Muslim. “The ten kingdoms are not Roman kingdoms; they are Muslim kingdoms, stretching from Morocco to Pakistan,” he maintains. 马克·埃利斯 作为10岁的男孩,马克·戴维森的母亲给了他Hal Lindsey的书"晚大星球地球"(The Late Great Planet Earth),这本书最终售出约3500万份,被纽约时报宣布为1970年代最畅销的非小说书籍. 该书对戴维森影响很大,塑造了他对"圣经预言"末期最早的看法.

受到911事件的震撼,退休的航空航天工程师戴维森更深入地挖掘了末日的预言,寻找世界事件方向的答案. 当他潜入与预言相关的圣经时,他发展了一个与传统教义在几个方面有所区别的框架,并由此产生了他的书:丹尼尔重温:发现四个中东部的标志导致反基督.

他对时事的教导中最相关的是他对伊朗的看法. 根据他对Daniel 7,Daniel 8 and Revelation 6的研究,Davidson确定了四大事件,他认为这四大事件是“标志性人物”,他认为,在Tribulation事件之前,在中东将展开。 这四个路标都将属于伊斯兰范畴.

“这一解释涉及丹尼尔七世的四只野兽、丹尼尔八世的公羊和山羊,以及启示录六世的四匹马。”

“他们都在谈论相同的四个事件, 他表示,第一个路标在伊拉克政府在2003年到2005年间更换时就已经实现,他现在认为,涉及霍尔木兹海峡的伊朗冲突与破坏可能表明第二个路标正在开始展开。 第二个路标是伊朗(Shia)攻击逊尼派邻国。

“在某种程度上,伊朗将摧毁沙特阿拉伯、科威特、阿联酋、卡塔尔和伊拉克的其余阿拉伯石油基础设施。” Davidson根据他的解释预测。 “他们已经告诉美国。

以及以色列,如果你攻击和摧毁我们的能源基础设施,我们将对所有其他邻国也这样做。 根据双方领导人的声明,袭击可能迫在眉睫。 “伊朗威胁在11月3日之前这样做,

“因此,爆炸可能很快发生。 但这就是我所看到的:美国和以色列会攻击伊朗。 伊朗会像以前一样, 摧毁其他阿拉伯基础设施, 经济混乱和混乱有可能威胁到美国作为世界储备货币的地位。

Davidson认为,“伊朗将夺走整个地球的心灵安宁”。 “人们会怀疑他们如何将食物放在桌子上。” 大卫森写了他的书来警告教会,因为他认为第二个路标会很糟糕. “这将会是可怕的。 这将会改变我们的生活, 改变我们在美国的生活方式,

马克·戴维森 “第二个路标将击中我们的脸。 我感到非常恐怖,并且惊慌失措地说,美国总统会触发第二个路标。 我很惊讶 " 这是整个潘多拉的盒子,一旦发生第二个路标,就会导致第三个路标,从而导致第四个路标,从而导致三难.

因此,上帝所做的是,他利用川普总统来触发路标,引发反基督派的到来,引发世界末日,引发基督的回归. 如果戴维森建议特朗普总统,他会告诉他尽快撤出美军. 戴维森认为重建犹太圣殿将在第三个路标上进行.

他偏离了传统教义,认为即将到来的反基督者将是阿拉伯叙利亚穆斯林。 他认为,“这十个王国不是罗马王国;它们是穆斯林王国,从摩洛哥延伸到巴基斯坦。” 有些人在Davidson的网站上发表评论,
